title: Australian Government delivers more mental health services for young Western Australians
text: Media event date: 6 September 2026 Date published: 6 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is expanding access to free mental health care in Western Australia, with a major upgrade to services in Perth's east and a brand-new centre for Perth's growing northern suburbs. Young people and families in Midland and the City of Wanneroo will soon have greater access to free mental health support closer to home, with Headspace Midland set to be upgraded and a new headspace centre to be delivered in Wanneroo. The existing headspace Midland centre, which has already delivered approximately 9,000 free appointments to local young people, will be upgraded to a headspace Plus centre, delivering enhanced support for those with more severe and complex mental health needs. As one of the first 10 headspace services in the country to transition to the new model of care, the Australian Government will deliver a new larger centre for headspace in Midland, expand the workforce of mental health professionals and increase the centre's capacity to support young people and families. A new headspace centre will also be established in the City of Wanneroo, bringing free mental health support to one of Perth's fastest-growing communities. The service will support young people aged 12 to 25 experiencing anxiety, depression, psychological distress and other mental health challenges, making it easier to access care when it's needed most. Both headspace Plus Midland and headspace Wanneroo are expected to open in the next financial year. headspace is Australia's leading youth mental health service and now the world's largest youth mental health network, with 176 centres operating nationwide. The Australian Government has committed more than $211.5 million to deliver 56 new, upgraded or expanded headspace services across Australia, including upgrading 30 centres to the headspace Plus model and expanding the network to more than 200 locations. For young people who prefer digital support eheadspace provides free online and telephone support, making sure help is available wherever they live. For more information, visit www.headspace.org.au or call 1800 650 890. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister, Emma McBride: “Around two in five young Australians experience mental health challenges every year, which is why early access to support is so important. “The upgrade of headspace Midland and the establishment of a new headspace centre in Wanneroo will help more young people access free mental health care in their local community. “The Albanese Labor Government is expanding access to free mental health services across Western Australia, ensuring more young people can get support early, before their mental health challenges become more serious.” Quotes attributable to Member for Hasluck, Tania Lawrence MP: “I think most of us know a young person who, at some point, has struggled and needed someone to talk to. "Headspace in Midland has provided a trusted and much loved listening ear and support for young people across Hasluck and beyond. "Now, to be delivering this investment to expand Headspace into Headspace Plus will mean services are even easier to access when young people's needs become more complex". "It’s about making sure a young person who is doing it tough can walk through the door and know: someone is here to help me. "Sitting alongside the Midland Kids Mental Health Hub and Midland Medicare Mental Health Centre for adults, the Albanese Labor Government's practical investment in mental health care is delivering services for all ages and needs in Hasluck". Quotes attributable to Member for Pearce, Tracey Roberts MP: "The City of Wanneroo is one of Perth's largest and fastest-growing communities, and it's important our young people have mental health support close to home." "For years, families in Pearce have had to travel to headspace Joondalup, one of the busiest centres in WA, just to access this kind of support." "This new centre means young people and families in Pearce will finally have somewhere local to turn to, while also taking pressure off headspace Joondalup." "This is Community First, backing our growing region with the services it needs, now and into the future." title: Health professionals invited to contribute to Australia's first perimenopause and menopause clinical guidelines
text: Media event date: 3 September 2026 Date published: 3 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is delivering Australia’s first perimenopause and menopause clinical guidelines to ensure women in Australia and healthcare professionals have trusted, evidence-based advice to support this important stage of life. The Government has engaged the Living Evidence Collaboration (ALEC) at Monash University to lead the development of Australia’s first national clinical guidelines for perimenopause and menopause. ALEC is currently seeking engagement from relevant health professional bodies. Perimenopause and menopause affect millions of Australian women and can have a significant impact on health, wellbeing and daily life. The new guidelines will provide healthcare professionals with evidence-based guidance to support women. The guidelines will be developed in partnership with the Australasian Menopause Society (AMS), the Endocrine Society of Australia (ESA), Jean Hailes for Women’s Health (Jean Hailes) and the Australian Academy of Health and Medical Sciences (AAHMS). Consultation and engagement will also be undertaken with peak health professional bodies across Australia whose members provide clinical care to women during perimenopause and menopause. Importantly, these 'living' guidelines will be regularly updated as new evidence emerges ensuring clinicians have access to the latest research and best-practice advice. The Australian Perimenopause and Menopause Guidelines will be developed in accordance with established National Health and Medical Research Council processes. The 2025–26 Budget provided funding of $2.9 million over three years from 2025–26 to support the development of the national guidelines. This work builds on the Australian Government’s landmark Women’s Health Package that includes new Medicare-supported menopause health assessments, cheaper menopause treatments through the PBS, 33 Endometriosis and Pelvic Pain Clinics delivering menopause and perimenopause care and Australia's first national Menopause and Australia’s first national Menopause and Perimenopause Awareness Campaign. For more information contact admin.alec@monash.edu or visit https://livingevidence.org.au/ . Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: “Women deserve access to trusted information and quality care throughout every stage of life. “These guidelines will give health professionals the evidence they need to better support women experiencing perimenopause and menopause. “This is another practical step in improving women’s health and helping women access informed, consistent care when they need it.” Quotes attributable to Professor Tari Turner, Academic Director, Australian Living Evidence Collaboration “ALEC is delighted to be collaborating with the Australasian Menopause Society, the Endocrine Society of Australia, Jean Hailes for Women's Health, the Australian Academy of Health and Medical Sciences, the broader health community and those with lived experience to contribute to the development of national, evidence-based guidelines for perimenopause and menopause. “Ensuring that healthcare decisions are grounded in high-quality research is at the heart of our mission, and we are delighted to help shape recommendations that will make a meaningful difference in women's health across the nation." title: $3 million boost to support men's health
text: Media event date: 2 September 2026 Date published: 2 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is investing $3 million to support the mental health and wellbeing of boys and men, by backing new research from Flinders University that responds to significant gaps in evidence and support for boys’ and men’s mental health. This investment will be used to help establish the ‘WellMen’: Centre for the Mental Health and Wellbeing of Boys and Men, which will be led by Professor James Smith of Flinders University. Professor Smith and his team are aiming to improve the mental health and wellbeing of boys and men in Australia by working with them to develop new strategies to promote mental health at critical life stages and in places where they feel most comfortable including schools, sports clubs, and online. The project will also lead to developing, supporting and growing the boys' and men's mental health promotion in the workforce. WellMen will be supported by a range of industry partners including the Movember Institute of Men’s Health, The Man Cave and Deadly Male. This funding forms part of a larger investment of $66 million under NHMRC’s Centre of Research Excellence (CRE) 2026 grant opportunity. The CRE scheme provides support for teams of researchers to pursue collaborative research and develop capacity in basic science research, clinical research, health services research and public health research. Read more about the projects funded on NHMRC’s website . Quotes attributable to Special Envoy for Men’s Health, Dan Repacholi MP: “The Australian Government is proud to support this important research that brings together leading researchers across various facets of men’s health into one integrated, multidisciplinary project. “Too many Australian men and boys are struggling with their mental health, and we need to do more to make sure support reaches them in the places and ways that work for them. “The WellMen CRE is a critical piece of the puzzle that will help us tackle the ongoing national crisis of men’s and boys’ mental health.” Quotes attributable to NHMRC CEO Professor Steve Wesselingh: “Health and medical research have the power to change lives by building the evidence we need to improve health outcomes for people across Australia. “Through NHMRC’s Centre of Research Excellence scheme, we are supporting high quality, collaborative research that can be translated into better policy, practice and care. “This investment will help build the skills, partnerships and research workforce needed to respond to priority health challenges, such as men’s and boys’ mental health and deliver lasting benefits for the community.” Quotes attributable to CRE Director, Professor James Smith: “WellMen intentionally brings together researchers, health professionals, policymakers, industry partners and consumers to co-design mental health research priorities that are critical for advancing boys and men’s mental health and wellbeing in Australia. “WellMen represents a critical milestone in men’s mental health research in Australia, with significant potential to shape mental health promotion and prevention investments that are appropriately tailored to the needs of boys and men, particularly those from marginalised backgrounds. “WellMen provides critical infrastructure to invest in the next generation of men’s mental health researchers in Australia, including stronger national and international research partnerships and co-ordination.” Quotes attributable to Movember Institute of Men’s Health Chief Impact Officer, Professor Simon Rice: “The WellMen CRE will create critical opportunities for capacity development and knowledge gain for men’s mental health scholarship and practice both here in Australia and internationally. The Movember Institute of Men’s Health is proud to be a partner in the CRE, including our direct role with two industry-based researchers embedded within the CRE work”. Quotes attributable to The Man Cave CEO, Ben Vasiliou : “Boys and men in Australia deserve a mental health system that is designed for them, not adapted for them as an afterthought. WellMen gives us a genuine chance to build that, and The Man Cave is ready to make that happen.” Quotes attributable to Deadly Male Board Director, Jason Bonson: “Deadly Male is delighted to be partnering with WellMen researchers to build a stronger evidence base and to support knowledge translation activities. “These activities are aimed at improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander male social and emotional wellbeing through community led research that informs strengths based and culturally relevant solutions.” Quotes attributable to nineteen year old Peter Susanto from the Northern Territory: “Investing in ‘WellMen’ does not just mean delivering crucial research to support evidence based, localised and sustainable solutions for creating well men - the ripple effect of boys and men living productive, healthy and peaceful lives benefits the entire community.” Minister: The Hon Dan Repacholi MP Tags: Men's health

title: Supporting better quality residential aged care
text: Media event date: 2 September 2026 Date published: 2 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Government is continuing to support the aged care sector to deliver better quality care for older Australians, with increases to vital funding taking effect in the coming weeks. From 1 October, the Australian National Aged Care Classification (AN-ACC) price will increase to $303.19 per resident, per day. This will provide more essential support for the more than 200,000 older people in residential aged care. This additional funding forms part of the Labor’s ongoing response to the recommendations of the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety, which called for a funding system that keeps pace with the real cost of care. For now, the hotelling supplement will remain at its current rate of $22.15 per resident, per day. This supplement helps providers cover everyday items like food, cleaning and laundry for residents. The Government requested IHACPA undertake a review of the hoteling supplement to ensure it supports the delivery of high-quality care that meets future demand. This review is currently underway and will inform Government decisions on any changes to the supplement. Labor will continue to invest to keep older Australians receiving the high quality, dignified care they deserve. This year, the Government will invest $47 billion in aged care. This includes our $1.7 billion investment in the 2026-27 Budget to support the sector to build 5,000 more aged care beds each year through added incentives. The average ‘per resident, per day’ care funding is now around 65 per cent higher than it was in September 2022. The Government will also maintain current care minute requirements and AN-ACC fixed and variable funding categories. This is based on the Independent Health and Aged Care Pricing Authority's (IHACPA) advice and aligns funding with the costs of residents' care across Australia. Quotes attributable to the Minister for Aged Care and Seniors, Sam Rae MP: “Making sure older Australians and their families have a quality, affordable and safe aged care system that is properly funded is a priority of the Albanese Government. “This announcement means more funding for aged care homes, supporting workers and better care for our loved ones.” Minister: The Hon Sam Rae MP Tags: Aged care

title: Delivering free mental health care for South Australians at every stage of life
text: Media event date: 2 September 2026 Date published: 2 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is delivering free mental health care across the lifespan for Australians – with two new centres officially opening in South Australia. Delivered in partnership with the South Australian Government, the Northern Adelaide Medicare Mental Health Centre and the Northern Adelaide Kids Hub have both started to support the local community. These services are about making sure every South Australian can access mental health care when they need it, regardless of their age, postcode or bank balance. Located at 7 Oldham Road, Elizabeth Vale, the Northern Adelaide Medicare Mental Health Centre will be staffed by a multidisciplinary team of 15 health professionals, including a psychiatrist, social workers, mental health nurses and peer workers. It joins a network of five Medicare Mental Health Centres in South Australia which have delivered more than 25,000 free walk in appointments. The Kids Hub is the second of its kind in South Australia and builds on a growing national network that is helping children and families access early intervention and support closer to home. Both services will provide free, high-quality mental health care without the need for a referral or appointment. The Australian Government has now delivered 57 Medicare Mental Health Centres across Australia, supporting more than 500,000 free walk-in appointments for people in their local communities. The Government is also delivering a national network of 17 Medicare Mental Health Kids Hubs, with the North Adelaide Kids Hub being the 16 th . People seeking information, advice or support can connect with Medicare Mental Health by calling 1800 595 212 or visiting www.medicarementalhealth.gov.au . Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister McBride: “The Albanese Labor Government is delivering free mental health care no matter your stage in life, post code or bank balance. “In partnership with Minister Boyer and the Malinauskas Government, these new services will make it easier for more South Australians to access high-quality care close to home. “Medicare Mental Health Centres across the country have already delivered more than 500,000 free walk-in appointments, with another 32 centres to be rolled out by 2030. “This is what strengthening Medicare means: making sure more Australians can get free mental health care, when and where they need it.” Quotes attributable to Minister Boyer: "Mental health care should be easy to access when people need it most, and these new services in Northern Adelaide will help ensure more South Australians can get the right support, closer to home. "By co-locating the Medicare Mental Health Centre with our Crisis Stabilisation Centre, we're creating a more connected system of care that helps people access support earlier and reduces the need for more acute interventions – easing pressure on our busy emergency departments. "This partnership with the Albanese Government is increasing mental health services in South Australia and making it easier for people to access the care and support they need." Quotes attributable to Member for Spence Matt Burnell: “Helping those in our community access free mental health care when they need it, has always been a priority for me since being elected. “We all know someone that has been through moments in life where it has been truly challenging, I am proud to be part of a Labor Government that is delivering a service, so our community has somewhere to turn to for support in their time of need. “We know more and more young people are presenting for mental health assistance, it is impacting them at a critical stage of their life and services they can turn have been limited. title: First national framework to strengthen health literacy
text: Media event date: 1 September 2026 Date published: 1 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Australians will be better supported to find, understand and use reliable health information, with the first National Health Literacy Framework launched today at the University of Sydney. Health literacy is vital life skill which gives people the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their health, from understanding when to get a screening test to knowing where to seek care and making sense of treatment options. Lower health literacy is linked with delayed care, higher hospital use, poorer chronic disease management, medication errors and avoidable hospitalisations. The framework provides the first nationally coordinated approach to improving health literacy in Australia. It offers evidence-based guidance to support the development of policies and programs by all levels of government, health services and community organisations to improve health literacy. The framework estimates that improving health literacy by 25% could save $7.3 billion annually. With Australians exposed to more health information that ever before, particularly through social media, online resources and artificial intelligence (AI), being able to identify information that is accurate and trustworthy is increasingly important. Importantly, the framework recognises that improving health literacy is not just the responsibility of individuals. Health services, information and systems must also be easier to access, understand and use. It also supports the delivery of culturally safe and inclusive health information and services for diverse communities, including First Nations peoples and multicultural communities who may face additional barriers to accessing care. The Australian Government provided funding to the Sax Institute and the Sydney Health Literacy Lab at the University of Sydney to develop the Framework as part of implementation of the National Preventive Health Strategy 2021–2030. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: “Health literacy gives people the confidence to understand their health and make informed decisions about their care “With more health information at our fingertips than ever before, particularly through social media and AI, knowing what information you can trust really matters. “People shouldn’t have to be health experts to understand their own health. This framework provides a national roadmap to help all people in Australia make informed health decisions and make sure health information is communicated clearly in a way that is easy to understand. " Quotes attributable to Professor Kirsten McCaffery, Director of the University of Sydney Health Literacy Lab: “Health literacy isn’t just about understanding information. It’s about knowing where to find information and who to trust. "There is a lot of useful health guidance available online and on social media, but there is also much that is misleading, false or linked to influencers with vested financial interests. “Helping Australians unpick what can be trusted and what should be scrutinised is vital – and is why we’re so pleased to have worked with government on the National Health Literacy Framework.” Quotes attributable to Saad Khalid, Chair of the Community Panel, Sydney Health Literacy Lab: "For many communities, especially migrant and multicultural communities like mine, it can be hard to know where to go for the right information. "Making sure that information and services are easy to find, understand and use will help people navigate the health system more easily and access the best possible guidance." Saad Khalid is a 24-year-old Pakistani-Australian and a nationally recognised leader in multicultural media and ethnic community broadcasting. A 2024 Young Australian of the Year finalist, he continues to advocate for migrant and multicultural communities through work spanning health, media, governance and public policy. He chairs CoSHeLL, the Sydney Health Literacy Lab’s Community Panel, and draws on his own lived experience to bring community experiences into the institutions and systems that shape people’s lives. title: McGrath Foundation adds prostate cancer nurses
text: Media event date: 31 August 2026 Date published: 31 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Government is providing $46.5 million over five years (2027-28 to 2031-32) to further expand the highly regarded McGrath Foundation Cancer Care Nurse service to include prostate cancer nurses from 1 July 2027. This funding will support 60.5 (FTE) prostate cancer nurse positions in health and hospital services around Australia. Male cancer incidence rates in Australia remain high, almost one in two Australian men will be diagnosed with cancer by age 85. As at 1st July 2026, the 128 new McGrath Cancer Care Nurses, placed since the McGrath Foundation announced it was taking its care to all cancers, had supported 7,522 patients nationally, comprising 4,200 males (56%) and 3,322 females (44%). This latest expansion of the McGrath service will add to existing Cancer Care Nurses which support a range of cancers including breast, gastrointestinal, gynaecologic, genitourinary, multi-tumour, lung and mesothelioma, brain, liver and bile, sarcoma, blood, head and neck, myeloma, melanoma and skin cancers. Prostate cancer represents around a third of all male cancer diagnoses, with more than 28,000 Australian men estimated to be diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2025. The Australian Government thanks the Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia (PCFA) which has delivered a successful, high-quality prostate cancer nursing service. The McGrath Cancer Care Nurses will continue to work with the PCFA Specialist Support Service, recognising the ongoing value of PCFA’s support, particularly in providing survivorship care for men living with and beyond prostate cancer. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “The Albanese Government is improving the wellbeing of all people impacted by cancer, including men. “We are strengthening nursing support and national system leadership by working with the McGrath Foundation to help more men affected by cancer." Quotes attributable to Dan Repacholi: “Today’s announcement is good news for Australian men diagnosed with prostate cancer and their families. “It highlights the government’s broader commitment to make sure men with cancer, regardless of cancer type, geography, cultural background or socioeconomic circumstances, get the care they need, where and when they need it.” Quotes attributable to Glenn McGrath, President & Co-Founder, McGrath Foundation: "We're incredibly grateful to the Federal Government for their continued commitment to equitable cancer care in Australia through the McGrath Cancer Care Nurse program. “With one in two Australians likely to be diagnosed with cancer in their lifetime, this announcement reflects what's possible when government, health services and the broader cancer sector work together with patients at the centre. “Together, we can ensure more men with prostate cancer can have access to the free, expert support of a McGrath Cancer Care Nurse." Quotes attributable to Kerry Patford, Chief Nurse, McGrath Foundation: "McGrath Cancer Care Nurses provide expert support throughout a person's cancer experience, helping people navigate treatment, make informed decisions and access the care they need. “Today’s announcement will help improve equity of access to cancer care by extending the McGrath Model of Care for All Cancers to support men with prostate cancer and their families." title: Consultation opens on proposed NDIS access changes
text: Media event date: 31 August 2026 Date published: 31 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Australians are invited to help shape proposed changes to how people access the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). Consultation is now open on changes that will help make NDIS access decisions clearer, fairer and more consistent. This includes considering how a person’s functional capacity is assessed, what evidence should be used to support access decisions, and how future access decision-making processes could be designed. The views and experiences of people with disability, families, carers, advocates, disability service providers and health professionals will inform the work of the Technical Advisory Group for NDIS functional capacity (TAG). This feedback will guide the TAG’s independent, evidence-based advice to governments. The TAG was established in July 2026 to support access reforms and strengthen the way NDIS access decisions are made. It is co-convened by the Commonwealth Minister for Health, Disability and Ageing, the Hon Mark Butler MP, and the ACT Minister for Disability, Carers and Community Services, Ms Suzanne Orr MLA. The NDIS Review found the current access process can be unclear and inconsistent, including how access rules are applied in relation to permanence of disability and how disability affects a person’s everyday life. These reforms will introduce a standardised approach to assessing functional capacity and move away from diagnosis as the primary means of determining NDIS eligibility. The consultation forms part of broader reforms to make the NDIS stronger, fairer and more sustainable, and return the scheme’s focus to the people it was designed to support – those with permanent and significant disability. Consultation is open from 31 August to 2 October 2026. To make a submission, visit consultations.health.gov.au. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “A strong and sustainable NDIS relies on people having confidence that the scheme is supporting those in our community who need it most. “This consultation is an opportunity for people with disability and the broader community to help shape a more transparent and consistent NDIS access process. “These reforms will secure the NDIS for future generations, ensuring it can continue to provide vital support to those who rely on it for decades to come.” Quotes attributable to Minister McAllister: “The best reforms are shaped by the people they affect, and this consultation is an opportunity to do just that. “I want to hear from people with disability on how they want the proposed changes to look and operate. Their input is invaluable. “I am particularly keen to hear from people from a diverse range of backgrounds and communities.” Quotes attributable to TAG Co-Convenor Minister Suzanne Orr: “To be effective and sustainable, the work of the Technical Advisory Group must be informed by the experience and needs of people with disability, their families, carers and all who support them. “I welcome the opportunity for community input to inform and guide the independent.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP Senator the Hon Jenny McAllister Tags: Disability and carers

title: Expansion of immunotherapy PBS listing to treat multiple new cancers
text: Media event date: 30 August 2026 Date published: 30 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Government is continuing to deliver cheaper medicines with thousands more Australians to benefit from an immunotherapy cancer treatment on the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS). From September 1, Pembrolizumab (Keytruda®) is being significantly expanded as a multi-cancer listing for Australians living with advanced and high-risk cancers. Keytruda has already been listed on the PBS for 17 cancer indications, now clinicians will have the option of prescribing the treatment for additional advanced cancers including: Advanced cholangiocarcinoma (Bile duct cancer) Ovarian cancer Merkel cell carcinoma (a rare skin cancer) Advanced or metastatic cancer occurs when the disease has spread from its original site to nearby tissues, lymph nodes or other parts of the body. Keytruda® works by blocking a pathway that cancer cells use to hide from the immune system, helping the body to recognise and attack the cancer. Around 700 Australians per year are expected to benefit from this listing. Without the PBS subsidy, patients might pay around $14,800 per script. Separately, Keytruda has also been newly listed in combination with the drug Enfortumab Vedotin (Padcev®) for the treatment of patients with Stage 3 or 4 urothelial cancer. This is an advanced form of bladder cancer where the cancer has spread beyond the bladder to nearby tissues, lymph nodes or other parts of the body. Padcev® in combination with Keytruda® provides a targeted treatment option by directly targeting cancer cells and helping the immune system attack the disease. More than 490 Australians are expected to benefit from this listing each year. Without PBS subsidy, patients might pay up to $4,800 per script. Since July 2022, the Australian Government has approved extra funding for 492 new and amended listings on the PBS. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “This expanded PBS listing of Keytruda, to cover multiple cancers will mean thousands more Australian patients can get the treatment they need faster and at an affordable price. “Keytruda is one of the most extraordinary drugs available in the country and now it is listed to help so many more Australian patients. “This is another illustration of the beauty of our Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme, bringing the best medicines in the world, to Australia at affordable prices.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP Tags: Medicines

title: Thousands expected to access free mental healthcare through new GC centre
text: Media event date: 27 August 2026 Date published: 27 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public More than 6,000 Gold Coast residents are expected to access free mental health care over the next 12 months following the official opening of the new Northern Gold Coast Medicare Mental Health Centre in Pimpama. Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Emma McBride MP joined Senator Murray Watt to officially launch the service, marking a significant investment in mental health support for one of Australia's fastest-growing regions. Located at 27 Dixon Drive, Pimpama, the centre will provide free, walk-in mental health care and support for people experiencing mental health challenges or psychological distress without the need for a referral or booking. As the northern corridor of the Gold Coast continues to experience rapid population growth, the new service will help make sure local residents can access timely and professional support close to home when they need it most. The centre will be home to a team of 24 staff, including 20 highly trained mental health professionals who will deliver free care and support. The Northern Gold Coast Medicare Mental Health Centre builds on the success of the Medicare Mental Health network across Queensland, where nearly 80,000 free walk-in appointments have already been delivered. Jointly funded by the Australian and Queensland Governments, the Pimpama centre is the 17th Medicare Mental Health Centre in Queensland and forms part of a growing national network of 57 centres helping Australians access free mental health care in their local communities. The centre has been commissioned by the Gold Coast Primary Health Network and operated by Open Minds. People seeking information, advice or support can connect with Medicare Mental Health by calling 1800 595 212 or visiting www.medicarementalhealth.gov.au . Quotes attributed to Assistant Minister McBride: “Today’s announcement means locals on the Gold Coast will have access to free mental health care when they need it. “We know one in five adults experience mental health challenges every year, and now those people will be able to access free mental health care through a psychologist, counsellor, social worker and or peer worker at the Northern Gold Coast Medicare Mental Health Centre. “The Albanese Labor Government is continuing to expand our network of Medicare Mental Health Centres to make sure that no one is left behind.” Quotes attributed to Queensland Minister for Health and Ambulance Services Tim Nicholls: “The Crisafulli Government is committed to building a stronger mental health system that gives Queenslanders easier access to health services when they need them. “We are investing significantly in the mental health workforce, infrastructure and services across Queensland, to meet the demand from our growing population, particularly in booming areas like the northern Gold Coast.” Quotes attributed to Senator Watt: “It’s great to see this fantastic new health service delivered for Gold Coasters, especially for the growing northern corridor. “Since they opened, locals have really embraced the Albanese Government’s Medicare Urgent Care Clinics for after-hours bulk-billed medical support, and today marks another step forward for Gold Coast health services. “Access to good, affordable mental health assistance can make a world of difference for a person in need, as well as their family and community, so it’s excellent to see this facility open here in Pimpama.” Minister: The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Mental health and suicide prevention

title: $10K incentives backing more Tasmanians into a trade
text: Media event date: 26 August 2026 Date published: 26 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public More than 800 Tasmanians have kickstarted their pathway to a trade, and with it a good, secure career for their future, backed in by the Albanese Labor Government’s $10,000 incentives for new housing construction apprentices. In the first 13 months of the Key Apprenticeship Program, 801 Tasmanians joined the program, signing up as new apprentices in the housing construction sector and growing the skills pipeline to help build more homes for Tasmanians. Supported by 453 employers across the state, the apprentices will receive five $2,000 incentive payments over the life of their apprenticeship to help with costs such as tools and transport, while also supporting apprentices to stick with their apprenticeship through to completion. Chippies are proving to be the most popular occupations in Tasmania, with 347 apprentice commencements in the program, followed by plumbers (122 commencements) and glaziers, plasterers and tilers (77 commencements). More than half of apprentices are aged 19 or under, showing strong interest from young Tasmanians in building a career in the trades. The industry is also seeing a greater diversity of apprentices starting in critical, home-building trades, with 42 female apprentices backed through the program so far. At 5%, this represents a promising start in growing the number of women in the industry, which more broadly sees around 3% of women working on the tools. Employers also benefit through the program, receiving $5,000 in the first year of the apprenticeship. Around 90% of these employers are small and medium-sized businesses. The Albanese Government is continuing to back apprentices and employers through the Key Apprenticeship Program, with the 2026–27 Budget locking in the program until 2029, including targeted incentives from 2027 for small and medium-sized businesses and Group Training Organisations. Visit www.apprenticeships.gov.au to learn more about the program. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White, MP for Lyons: "We need more homes in Tasmania and to build them we need more tradies, which is why our Government is focused on growing the pipeline of skilled workers we need. “It is fantastic to see more than 800 Tasmanians taking up an apprenticeship, including so many young people choosing a trade and building the skills for a good, secure career. "These incentives help with the real costs of starting an apprenticeship, like buying tools and getting to and from work, while also supporting the local businesses that employ and train our next generation of tradies. “Through the Key Apprenticeship Program and Free TAFE, we’re backing aspiring tradies throughout their journey into the industry and beyond.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: About the department

title: Permanent Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre to deliver ongoing support
text: Media event date: 26 August 2026 Date published: 26 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Labor Government is making sure ongoing access to free mental health support is available for the Bondi community, with the permanent Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre now officially open. In the immediate aftermath of the Bondi tragedy, the Albanese Government moved to provide dedicated mental health support for the community, including the Jewish community and all those affected by the terrorist attack. As part of a $42.9 million mental health support package, the Government established a temporary Medicare Mental Health Centre with a focus on trauma-informed care, while work began on a permanent service for the community. Today, Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Emma McBride joined the Member for Kingsford Smith, Matt Thistlethwaite, to officially open the new centre. Located at 241 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction, the Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre will provide free, walk-in mental health care and support for people experiencing distress, mental health concerns or emotional difficulties – no referral or appointment required. The centre will continue to deliver trauma-focused, support while serving as an open door for anyone in the community seeking help. For people who were visiting Bondi at the time of the attack and want to access support close to home, support is also available through the Government's growing network of Medicare Mental Health Centres across Australia. There are currently 57 centres open nationwide, with the network expanding to 92 locations. The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre has been commissioned by Central and Eastern Sydney Primary Health Network and is operated by New Horizons. People seeking support can walk in, call 1800 595 212, or visit www.medicarementalhealth.gov.au . Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “In the wake of the horrific Bondi terror attack, our Government swiftly put in place a range of services to provide immediate mental health and trauma support for the community. “The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre is one of those services, and a now permanent fixture to ensure mental health supports are accessible to those who need them, for years to come.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister McBride: “Following the senseless terrorist attack at Bondi last year, the Australian Government acted quickly to provide free and immediate mental health support for those affected. “The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre has played an important role in helping members of the community impacted by the attack, and this permanent centre will make sure that high-quality mental health care and support remains available for years to come. “Whether you're experiencing mental health challenges, emotional distress, or supporting a loved one, this centre provides a safe, welcoming and accessible place to seek help. “I want to thank the dedicated staff who have supported the Bondi community with compassion and care through an incredibly difficult period, and who will continue to provide that vital support from this new permanent location.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister Thistlethwaite: “This permanent Medicare Mental Health Centre will make sure people in our community have ongoing access to free, high‑quality mental health support close to home. “Whether someone is dealing with trauma, struggling with their wellbeing, or simply needs to talk to a professional, they’ll be able to walk in and get help without delay. “I want to thank the staff who have supported our community through an incredibly difficult time, and who will continue to provide that care from this new centre. This service will be an important part of Bondi’s recovery and a vital resource for our local area.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Mental health and suicide prevention

title: Clinical roundtable to focus on women's cardiovascular health
text: Media event date: 24 August 2026 Date published: 24 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Women’s experiences of cardiovascular disease have been put at the centre of discussions with clinicians and researchers. This is the second roundtable held as part of the Ministerial Expert Panel on Women’s Health that is initially focusing on women’s cardiovascular health. Clinical stakeholders were brought together to discuss improvements across prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for women across Australia. More than 70 people attended the clinical roundtable, from diverse backgrounds, across clinical practice, research, consumer advocacy, primary care, specialist care, professional colleges and Aboriginal Community-Controlled Health Services. The roundtable looked at where women are missing out, from understanding their risk and recognising the warning signs of a heart attack or stroke, to the barriers women face in getting the right diagnosis and treatment. We heard from a range of committed organisations including Royal Australian College of General Practitioners, Australian College of Rural and Remote Medicine, National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation and peak bodies such as the Heart Foundation and Stroke Foundation. It follows a recent consumer roundtable where women shared their own experiences of cardiovascular disease and care, including the importance of having their symptoms heard and taken seriously and accessing timely treatment and follow-up care. Cardiovascular disease and stroke remain major health issues for women. More than half a million women in Australia are diagnosed with cardiovascular disease each year. In 2023, nearly 40,000 women had a heart attack, unstable angina or a stroke and 262,000 women were hospitalised with cardiovascular disease. In 2023-24, First Nations women had higher prevalence, hospitalisation and death rates due to cardiovascular disease and CVD subtypes when compared to non-Indigenous Australians with the disparity greater among females. First Nations women also had higher rates for heart failure and cardiomyopathy, and for acute rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease than First Nations men. The insights from both roundtables will inform the Expert Panel’s advice to the Albanese Government on improving women’s cardiovascular health. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: “We want women to better understand their heart health and risks for stroke, know the signs that something isn’t right and feel confident their symptoms will be recognised and understood by health professionals. “We’ve heard directly from women about their experiences and now we’ve brought together health professionals and experts from across Australia to listen, learn and look at what needs to change to improve heart health diagnosis, treatment and care for women. “Telling women to take a mild pain relief or reduce their stress when they are experiencing significant symptoms of cardiovascular disease is not good enough. Every woman should feel confident that when something doesn’t feel right, she will be listened to, taken seriously and get the care she needs. “I thank the roundtable participants for sharing their expertise and experience and bringing their positivity and passion to an area of women’s health that has been under-recognised and underdiagnosed for too long.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Women's health

title: More than 200,000 visits to Medicare Urgent Care Clinics take pressure off Tasmanian hospitals
text: Media event date: 21 August 2026 Date published: 21 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Labor Government’s network of 8 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics have made it easier for hundreds of thousands of Tasmanians to get free urgent care from a doctor or nurse. There have now been over 200,000 free visits to Medicare Urgent Care Clinics across Tasmania since the first clinic opened in Launceston in June 2023. More than one in four of those visits to Tasmanian Urgent Care Clinics have been on the weekend, and one in three weekday visits have been after 5pm. We know that many Tasmanians who presented to an Urgent Care Clinic say they would have otherwise visited an Emergency Department at one of Tasmania’s hospitals. The network of 8 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics is just one way the Albanese Labor Government is helping take press off Tasmanian hospitals which also includes: Additional $700 million in funding for Tasmania’s hospitals Improving access to bulk billing doctors across the state We’ve made Urgent Care Clinics a permanent part of Medicare, because every Tasmanian should have access to free, quality healthcare close to home. Medicare Urgent Care Clinics allow people to access care outside of standard hours, providing an alternative to emergency departments for urgent but not life-threatening care. Medicare Urgent Care Clinics are open seven days a week, extended hours and offer walk-in care that is fully bulk billed – all you need is your Medicare card. To find a Medicare Urgent Care Clinic near you and what services they have available, visit: https://www.health.gov.au/find-a-medicare-ucc Quotes attributable to Minister Collins: “The sheer number of Tasmanians who have now visited a Medicare Urgent Care Clinic in our state – enough to fill UTAS stadium more than 10 times – underscores just how serious our government is about improving healthcare. “I am proud of the high quality, walk-in care that our state’s network of Medicare Urgent Care Clinics continue to deliver to Tasmanians. "Reaching the milestone of 200,000 visits to Medicare Urgent Care Clinics means hundreds of thousands of Tasmanians got the urgent care they needed, without waiting for hours in a hospital emergency department – and all they needed is their Medicare card. “Our investments into Medicare Urgent Care Clinics is just one way our government is strengthening Medicare, including making medicines cheaper and delivering more bulk billed GP visits.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister Rebecca White: "For families across Tasmania, having access to free urgent care in their community can make a real difference, particularly when someone they love is unwell or injured. "More than 200,000 visits shows the important role Medicare Urgent Care Clinics are playing in our communities across Tasmania, helping people get the care they need while easing pressure on our busy emergency departments. "Labor created Medicare because we believe every Australian deservers access to quality and timely healthcare. We're proud to keep strengthening Medicare, so it continues to deliver for families and communities in Tasmania." Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Medicare

title: Government delivers half a million free mental health appointments
text: Media event date: 20 August 2026 Date published: 20 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public More Australians than ever are accessing free mental health support, with Medicare Mental Health Centres delivering more than 500,000 walk-in appointments nationwide as the Government continues to strengthen Medicare. In 2025-26, almost 24,000 people accessed support through Medicare Mental Health Centres on more than 230,000 occasions. Without Medicare Mental Health Centres, many of these Australians would have faced out-of-pocket costs for care or may not have sought support at all. In total, nearly 50,000 Australians have now turned to Medicare Mental Health Centres for free mental health support, with most presenting for anxiety and mild depression. Medicare Mental Health Centres provide immediate support without the need for a referral or pre-booked appointment, making it easier for Australians to get help when they need it, where they are. To make sure no Australian misses out, the Government is continuing to expand the Medicare Mental Health Centre network, with an additional $267.3 million invested to rollout 32 new or upgraded centres taking the network to 92 across Australia by mid-2030. Staffed by highly trained teams of psychologists, counsellors, social workers, mental health nurses and peer workers, the centres provide a welcoming place where Australians can access free support close to home. For further information on Medicare Mental Health Centres, visit the Medicare Mental Health website or call 1800 595 212. Quotes attributed to Minister Butler: “The Albanese Government is making it easier for Australians to receive the support and care they need when they need it. “No appointment needed, our Medicare Mental Health Centres are providing free face-to-face care to hundreds of thousands of Australians. Quotes attributed to Assistant Minister McBride: “In the past, Australians had to wait, travel and pay for vital mental health care. “Now by strengthening Medicare, the Albanese Labor Government has delivered 501,579 free walk-in appointments through Medicare Mental Health Centre - making it easier for people to get free, high-quality mental health care close to home. “Without Medicare Mental Health Centres, many of these Australians would have faced out-of-pocket costs for care or worse, may not have sought support at all. “The Albanese Labor Government has invested an additional $267.3 million to expand the Medicare Mental Health Centre network to 92 centres nationwide, so more Australians can access support without a referral, appointment or out-of-pocket cost.” Quotes attributed to Member for Canberra Alicia Payne: “Canberra’s Medicare Mental Health Centres are providing transformational support to people who need it most. “The Albanese Labor Government has ensured that mental health support is accessible when people need it both in terms of affordability and timely availability. “I’m proud to be part of a government that is prioritising free and easy to access mental health care for all Australians.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Mental health and suicide prevention

title: Certainty for older Australians and aged care providers on CHSP
text: Media event date: 20 August 2026 Date published: 20 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government will extend the Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP) to 30 June 2029 – giving 830,000 older Australians certainty about the services they use every day and supporting providers to continue critical aged care services. CHSP is the entry point for many older Australians to aged care. It provides supports like cleaning, shopping, meals on wheels, transport, home maintenance, social support and allied health. By extending these contracts, we are providing security for providers, including councils across Australia to continue providing these services. Local councils and other providers have cited uncertainty as their reason for withdrawing from CHSP. That excuse no longer exists. Councils’ contracts will continue without interruption until 2029 and older people in those communities are entitled to expect their services will continue. This extension will support around 1,300 providers to deliver CHSP services, including state and local governments, not for profit organisations and community groups. Many of them operate in regional, rural and remote communities where they are the only provider available. Almost 40 per cent of CHSP clients live outside the major cities. The Australian Government believes CHSP should remain a standalone program, rather than rolling it into Support at Home. We’ll use this extension to strengthen the program so it better delivers for older Australians. We want the CHSP program to be sustainable and better integrated with Support at Home to deliver a holistic home care program and will begin consultation this year on a long-term future for the program, including how block funding can be continued, ensuring fair and equitable contributions to the costs of home care and how early intervention services can reduce pressure across the system. Quotes attributable to Minister for Health and Ageing, the Hon Mark Butler MP “I know how much this program means to older Australians, their families and communities. “We have listened to the feedback people have given us about CHSP, and we’re giving providers and older Australians the certainty they need to continue while the future of the program is developed." Quotes attributable to Minister for Aged Care and Seniors, the Hon Sam Rae MP "830,000 older Australians rely on these services – today we’re giving them the certainty they need that their care will not change while we plan for the future of CHSP. "We said we would listen before we made decisions about the future of this program. Providers told us they needed certainty to keep their doors open, and older people told us they wanted continuity – and we’ll continue to listen as we deliver the program people want into the future. "Block funded, community based services do something Support at Home was never designed to do - they keep people well and independent before they need more intensive support. There is a continuing role for that system and we are going to design it properly, with the people who deliver it and the people who use it." Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Sam Rae MP Tags: Aged care

title: New select committee to continue focus on women's health
text: Media event date: 19 August 2026 Date published: 19 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Senate has today agreed to establish a Senate Select Committee on women’s health, following a motion moved by Senator Marielle Smith. A new Select Committee in the Senate, chaired by Senator Smith, will elevate women's voices and experiences by holding public hearings across Australia. The new Select Committee will have a strong focus on women’s health issues including fertility, postpartum healthcare and women’s pain. This work builds on the Albanese Labor Government’s work to deliver more choice, lower costs and better care for women and girls in Australia. Our landmark investment of nearly $800 million in women's health has meant that hundreds of thousands of women have saved money on essential medicines, more women are getting dedicated endometriosis and menopause care and access to long-acting contraception is easier and more affordable. The Government is also delivering support for First Nations women and families through our investments in Birthing on Country and First Nations Maternal and Child Health Models that support women to access culturally appropriate care in community. Assistant Minister for Health and Ageing and Assistant Minister for Women, Hon. Rebecca White MP looks forward to receiving the recommendations of the final report and considering how they may inform future policy development. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Health and Ageing, Rebecca White MP: "The Albanese Government has made women's health a national priority, investing nearly $800 million to deliver more choice, lower costs and better care for women across Australia. "Every woman’s experience of healthcare is different and it’s important we listen to women and their families about their reproductive journey including their experiences of pregnancy loss and postpartum care. “I encourage women, families, organisations and advocates to share their experiences and insights, so we can continue to improve care and support for women across Australia.” Quotes attributable to Senator Marielle Smith, Senator for South Australia. “I am grateful to have the support of the Senate to establish this committee and thank my fellow Senators who voted in support of it. “I am determined to use the powerful spotlight of the Senate to continue to bring women's lived experiences into the light, so we can drive the change that they deserve. “Too many women are suffering in the postpartum period. Too many are sitting in a darkness that can feel all consuming. We cannot leave them to face this alone. “I am determined to use my role in the Senate to continue driving change in women's health and am firmly of the belief that this is the next frontier that we must tackle with urgency. “We know from the Senate Inquiry into Issues related to Menopause and Perimenopause, that by overcoming stigma and bringing lived experience into the light, change is possible. “This committee will provide a space for women to share their experiences, and have their voices heard.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Emma McBride: “We know that around one in five new and expectant mothers experience perinatal depression or anxiety, and many never receive the support they need. “That’s why the Albanese Government has made perinatal mental health a priority, including investing in a national network of dedicated perinatal mental health centres. But we know there is more work to do. “We must build on the systems already in place to make sure every woman can navigate pregnancy and early parenthood with confidence, knowing support is only a small step away. “This inquiry is an important opportunity to hear directly from women and families about their experiences, identify gaps in care, and make sure women receive the support they deserve right across out healthcare system.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Women's health

title: Legislation to secure the future of the NDIS passed by the Senate
text: Media event date: 18 August 2026 Date published: 18 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Government has secured the future of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), with legislation to make the scheme safer, clearer and more sustainable for participants, passed by the Senate today. The NDIS Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Bill 2026 delivers on key reforms to strengthen the scheme and ensure it can continue supporting people with permanent and significant disability. This includes changes to clarify how support determinations work and who they apply to, as well as outlining safeguards for participants who require continuous 24-hour care. The changes also clarify eligibility requirements, improve how NDIS plans are managed and administered, provide clearer rules about how funding can be used, strengthen oversight of providers delivering NDIS-funded supports and strengthen fraud and integrity measures. The Bill was shaped by feedback from people with disability and their families and carers, as well as advocates, providers and the broader disability community, including through the Senate inquiry. The government agreed to several amendments to strengthen participant safeguards, make the laws clearer and easier to understand, and support new arrangements for plan management providers. Together, these reforms will help make the NDIS stronger, fairer and more sustainable, and return the scheme’s focus to the people it was designed to support – those with permanent and significant disability. Current NDIS access and planning arrangements will remain in place until changes are introduced gradually over the next few years. There will be no changes to access until 1 January 2028. The NDIA will communicate with participants before changes affect them. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “The NDIS is one of Australia’s most important social reforms, and this legislation is about strengthening the scheme so it can continue to deliver on its promise.” “These reforms will help make the NDIS safer, clearer and more sustainable, with stronger rules, better safeguards and greater confidence that funding is directed to the supports participants need.” “This is responsible reform that protects the integrity of the scheme while keeping people with disability at the centre of the NDIS.” Quotes attributable to Minister McAllister: “Passing this legislation is an important step, but our work does not stop here.” “This is a comprehensive package of reform which will deliver an NDIS which is strong, safe, sustainable and has a strong social license.” “We’ll be working with the disability community, their families, carers and the sector more broadly to implement these reforms and set the NDIS up for the long term.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP Senator the Hon Jenny McAllister Tags: Disability and carers

title: NDIS banning orders ramp up as record number of shonks kicked off scheme
text: Media event date: 17 August 2026 Date published: 17 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Government is stepping up efforts to tackle NDIS fraud and misconduct, protect people with disability and safeguard vital taxpayer-funded disability supports. Between April and June 2026, the NDIS Quality and Standards Commission issued 111 banning orders to individuals, registered providers and unregistered providers. This is the highest number of banning orders ever issued by the NDIS Commission in a single quarter. These banning orders have stopped convicted criminals, dodgy consultants, fraudsters and other high-risk individuals from operating in the NDIS and putting participants at risk. The record number of bans issued between April and June has pushed the total number of banning orders issued in 2026 to 158 so far, marking a 35 per cent increase on the same period last year. The NDIS Commission also refused the registration of 229 providers, and revoked the registration of 453 existing providers, preventing unsuitable providers and individuals from entering or remaining in the registered NDIS market. This increase in enforcement activity follows the passage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Integrity and Safeguarding) Act in April, which gave the NDIS Commission stronger powers to address fraud, misconduct and non-compliance in the scheme. Recent reforms announced by the Albanese Government requiring mandatory registration of supported independent living (SIL) and platform providers will further strengthen oversight of the sector, helping to reduce fraud and prevent unsuitable unregistered operators from participating in the NDIS market. Quotes attributable to Senator Jenny McAllister, Minister for the NDIS: “Working in the NDIS is a great privilege, and if you abuse that privilege you will be kicked out of the scheme. “The new powers we’ve legislated have given the NDIS Commission the strong powers it needed to really take the fight to the shonks and grifters who thought they could take advantage of one of our society’s most important social programs. “Every year, we are reviewing more claims, receiving more tip-offs, conducting more investigations, handing down more banning orders, referring more matters to the police and prosecuting more fraudsters.” Quotes attributable to NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commissioner Louise Glanville: “Providers who cannot demonstrate the capability, competence and quality standards required to support NDIS participants have no place in the Scheme. “Every banning order, registration refusal and revocation reflects our commitment to ensuring NDIS participants receive safe, high-quality supports from providers who meet their obligations.” Minister: Senator the Hon Jenny McAllister Tags: Disability and carers

title: Helping Australians reduce their dementia risk
text: Media event date: 14 August 2026 Date published: 14 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Dementia is the leading cause of death in Australia, but evidence shows nearly half of all cases can be delayed or prevented by addressing known risk factors. To help Australians combat these factors, the Australian Government has launched a new campaign to help Australians better understand their own dementia risk and make simple lifestyle changes early that could dramatically lower or delay their chances of developing the condition. Australians turning 50 will receive a letter to outline how they can reduce the risk of developing dementia and stay healthy for longer. The letters will go to roughly 340,000 people who turned 50 between 1 July 2025 and 30 June 2026, with the first letters having been sent from mid-July. The letters encourage Australians to eat healthily and stay active, limit alcohol, quit smoking, get their heart health and diabetes risk checked and keep their brain active among a range of other key factors crucial to their health. The letter was informed through engagement with leading dementia experts alongside world-leading research from the 2024 Lancet Commission on dementia. Recipients will also be able to get a free personal risk assessment and learn more about reducing their risk of dementia by visiting www.health.gov.au/dementia . Almost 460,000 Australians are currently estimated to be living with dementia, and this number expected to reach 1.1 million by 2065 as our population ages. The letter can be found on the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing’s website . Quotes attributable to the Minister for Health and Ageing, Mark Butler MP: “Dementia is a national health priority for our Government. “Growing evidence of risk factors for dementia show that the disease can be prevented or delay in around 45 per cent of cases. “That’s why we launched a campaign to help people better understand the risk factors, by sending a letter to every Australian when they turned 50. “50 year-olds who receive this letter will have guidance to better understand their risks, and what they can do to help reduce the chance of developing dementia.” Quotes attributable to the Minister for Aged Care and Seniors, Sam Rae MP: “Turning 50 is a great time to stop and think about your long-term health. These letters are a simple prompt to start a conversation every Australian should be having with loved ones and their doctor. "The science is clear that the choices we make in mid-life matter. Staying active, eating well and keeping on top of your heart health can help reduce your risk of developing dementia. “Reaching hundreds of thousands of Australians with practical advice is exactly what the National Dementia Action Plan tasks us with doing. Together we can bring dementia numbers down and give more older Australians longer, healthier lives.” Quotes attributable to the 2026 Senior Australian of the Year, Professor Henry Brodaty AO: "Australia has successfully tackled some of our biggest health challenges - from skin cancer and smoking to deaths from heart attacks. Now is the time to tackle dementia. "The evidence is in. Successful international trials, including our Maintain Your Brain trial, show that addressing dementia risk factors can improve cognitive abilities and delay decline. "We did ‘Slip, Slop, Slap’ for skin cancer. Now let’s do it for brain health." Quotes attributable to Dementia Australia CEO Professor Tanya Buchanan “It is never too early or too late to focus on your brain health. While we cannot change getting older, our genetics or family history, scientific research shows that looking after our brain health can make a big difference to reducing the risk of developing dementia. “Some of the modifiable risk factors for dementia surprise people, like taking action on hearing or vision loss, treating depression and staying socially connected. Making sure there are services and support to help people address risk factors is vitally important. “We know that many Australia’s still think dementia is a normal part of ageing. We need to continue to build awareness and brain health understanding across the community. The National Dementia Helpline is a great resource for people wanting to learn more about brain health. It operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, call 1800 100 500 or visit dementia.org.au” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Sam Rae MP Tags: Dementia

title: New Medicare Mental Health Centre to open in Tasmania
text: Media event date: 14 August 2026 Date published: 14 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is delivering more free mental health services for Tasmanians, with a new Medicare Mental Health Centre set to open in Glenorchy in the coming weeks. Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Emma McBride MP and Assistant Minister for Health and Aged Care, and Member for Lyons, Rebecca White MP, visited the centre ahead of its opening. Located at 388 Main Road, Glenorchy, the centre will deliver free, walk-in mental health support, with thousands of locals expected to access the service in its first year. A dedicated team of psychologists, counsellors, social workers and peer workers will deliver immediate and ongoing support, making it easier for people to get help close to home, without a referral or appointment. There are currently three Medicare Mental Health Centres operating across Tasmania, delivering almost 22,000 free walk in sessions since they were established. The Glenorchy centre will be the fourth, with five centres to be delivered statewide by 2030. The Glenorchy Medicare Mental Health Centre is part of the Albanese Labor Government's record $1 billion investment in mental health, making it easier for all Australians to access free mental health care close to home, when and where it’s needed most. The Glenorchy centre is funded by the Albanese Government, commissioned by Primary Health Tasmania and operated by Stride Mental Health. People seeking information or support can connect with Medicare Mental Health by calling 1800 595 212 or visiting www.medicarementalhealth.gov.au . Quotes attributed to Assistant Minister Emma McBride: "The Albanese Labor Government is strengthening Medicare by delivering more mental health services in the heart of local communities. “We know one in five Australians experiences mental ill-health each year. These are our family members, friends, neighbours and workmates. “That's why we're making it easier for Tasmanians to access free mental health support close to home, without the need for a referral or appointment, so they can get help when they need it most." Quotes attributed to Member for Lyons Rebecca White: "Everyone goes through difficult times and knowing where to turn for support can make all the difference. This new centre will give people a welcoming place to seek help close to home, when they need it most. "The centre will be open for people to walk in, no appointment needed, if they feel like speaking with someone about their mental health needs, and a reassuring reminding that no one has to manage with mental ill-health alone. "This centre is about making sure more Tasmanians can access free, compassionate support in their own community, giving people the confidence that help is there and recovery is possible." Quotes attributed to Senator Brown: “This centre is in the heart of Glenorchy right on the main Road. Mental health care should not be hidden away. Bringing these services out into the open helps break down stigma and makes asking for help a normal part of looking after your health.” “For people in Hobart’s northern suburbs, this is a direct investment in better health care close to home. Along with the new Medicare Urgent Care Clinic coming to Glenorchy, we are delivering more services locally so people can get the care they need, when they need it.” Minister: The Hon Emma McBride MP The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Mental health and suicide prevention

title: Strengthening Medicare: Bulk billing on the up
text: Media event date: 10 August 2026 Date published: 10 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government’s record investment in strengthening Medicare is delivering big benefits for Australians, with access to bulk billing continuing to increase way ahead of schedule. Nationally, the bulk billing rate for the June 2026 quarter rose to 84.1 per cent, up almost five percentage points on the same quarter, last year. Before the Albanese Government started investing in bulk billing, the national rate had fallen to 75.6 per cent. Bulk billing has increased in every state and territory: NSW 87.5% up 4.1 percentage points VIC 85.7%, up 5.7 percentage points QLD 82%, up 4.7 percentage points SA 82.5%, up 6 percentage points WA 76.8%, up 4.8 percentage points TAS 80.8%, up 5.5 percentage points NT 90.8%, up 13 percentage points and ACT 59.3%, up 2.4 percentage points. The bulk billing rate also for patients aged 16 to 64 years had the highest growth – up 8.2 percentage points to 78.6%. There are more than 3,800 Medicare Bulk Billing Practices, over 1,400 of those were mixed billing practices before our Government’s historic investments. A range of Medicare statistics are published quarterly on the Department’s website. Get more information on bulk billing including an additional bulk billing dashboard. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “Our government is delivering more bulk billing to more Australians “Across the country more and more GP practices are becoming fully bulk billing clinics meaning all patients need is their Medicare card, not their credit card. “It’s good for patients hip pockets and good for their health.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP Tags: Medicare Strengthening Medicare measures
