title: New clinical guidelines for detecting prostate cancer
text: Media event date: 7 August 2026 Date published: 7 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Australian men will benefit from new clinical practice guidelines on the early detection and management of prostate cancer. The new guidelines reflect the latest medical evidence and technological advances in prostate cancer diagnosis and management. They aim to support earlier detection, by focusing on each person’s risk of developing prostate cancer, while reducing the potential harms caused by overdiagnosis and overtreatment. The 2026 Clinical Guidelines for the Early Detection of Prostate Cancer replace the previous guidelines released in 2016. They were developed by the Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia in partnership with Cancer Council Australia with a $770,000 grant from the Australian Government. To support implementation of the guidelines, the government is providing $320,000 to the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners to develop and implement an education and awareness program for doctors. GPs are the first point of contact for men considering prostate cancer testing. The education program will help doctors to discuss relevant issues with their patients and support their patients to make informed decisions about testing, considering their individual risk, possible benefits and harms, and their values and preferences. Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in Australia, with around 28,000 men diagnosed annually, and almost 4,000 men losing their lives each year. The guidelines have been approved by the National Health and Medical Research Council and are available on the Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia website . Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “The new guidelines reflect the latest research and medical advances in prostate cancer. “The guidelines will ensure men and their families get the right support earlier.” Quotes attributable to Special Envoy Repacholi: “As co-chair of the government’s Prostate Cancer Expert Advisory Group which was established in March, I am committed to better detection, treatment, and care for Australian men with prostate cancer. “As the most commonly diagnosed cancer in Australia, prostate cancer has significant impacts on men, their families and the wider community. “I encourage any bloke aged 45 or more to have a chat with their doctor about whether they are at higher risk of prostate cancer and need to be tested.” Quotes attributable to Prof. Dorothy Keefe PSM MD, CEO Cancer Australia: “The new clinical guidelines will help maximise the early detection of prostate cancer in Australian men. “This approach closely aligns with the Australian Cancer Plan, which highlights the importance of personalised evidence-based early detection strategies. “The work by the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners to raise doctors’ awareness of the new guidelines is a critical step to ensure their effective implementation.” Quotes attributable to PCFA Chief Executive Anne Savage: “These Guidelines provide Australia with an extraordinary opportunity to reduce deaths from our most commonly diagnosed cancer.” “Realising that opportunity will require coordinated implementation, clinician education, consumer awareness, and ongoing investment in evidence-based care.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Dan Repacholi MP Tags: Cancer

title: More than 50,000 families supported to give their babies the best start in life
text: Media event date: 7 August 2026 Date published: 7 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is helping Australian families access trusted breastfeeding advice and support, with more than 50,000 families turning to the National Breastfeeding Helpline last year. As Australia marks World Breastfeeding Week, the National Breastfeeding Helpline and LiveChat Service continue to provide free, professional and non-judgemental support to parents and carers with feeding questions and breastfeeding challenges from pregnancy through to early childhood. Breastfeeding can give babies a strong start in life, supporting healthy growth and development and helping protect against a range of illnesses. It also has important health benefits for mothers, including reducing the risk of breast and ovarian cancers and supporting recovery after childbirth. While breastfeeding can be a rewarding experience, it is not always easy. Whether it is a late-night feeding concern, questions about milk supply or simply a need for reassurance, the National Breastfeeding Helpline connects families with trained counsellors who have breastfed themselves and understand the questions and pressures that can come with it. Operated by the Australian Breastfeeding Association, the National Breastfeeding Helpline and LiveChat Service are available 24 hours a day, helping parents and carers access evidence-based information, practical advice and support whenever they need it. Since 2008, the National Breastfeeding Helpline has received more than 1.2 million calls, making it one of Australia's most accessible sources of breastfeeding information and support. The service is delivered by 465 trained volunteer counsellors with personal breastfeeding experience. In the past 12 months, 43 per cent of callers reported the service helped them avoid a visit to a GP or other health service, showing how timely advice and reassurance can support families early. The Australian Government has funded the National Breastfeeding Helpline since 2008 and LiveChat since 2018 and is investing a further $8.9 million to ensure these services remain available to families across Australia. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White “Breastfeeding has lifelong benefits for both mothers and babies, but many parents need support along the way. Many parents have questions, especially in those early days and weeks, and it’s important they know support is available. “The National Breastfeeding Helpline gives families trusted, practical advice from trained counsellors who understand the challenges parents can face. “Whether you live in a major city, a regional town or a remote community, support is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.” Attributable to Australia Breastfeeding Association, Executive Officer, Victoria Marshall-Cerins “Every call and chat matters, our volunteers are available around the clock every day of the year. We provide a service that thousands of families rely on. “Calls are generally answered within 3 minutes by our incredible volunteers, many even sooner. It is a free service, families can call for reassurance, support, and care without having to leave the home.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Pregnancy, birth and baby

title: $180 million for First Nations health infrastructure
text: Media event date: 5 August 2026 Date published: 5 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Eligible Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations (ACCHOs) can now apply for a total of $180 million in grant funding from the Albanese Government to improve their clinical buildings and other infrastructure. This funding will support new buildings, as well as upgrades, repairs and maintenance to health infrastructure and housing for health professionals. New, fit-for-purpose buildings and spaces will improve access to culturally safe health care for First Nations people, and support workforce recruitment and retention. This funding builds on two previous grant rounds which supported the expansion and renewal of First Nations health infrastructure across Australia. On average, completed projects report a 15 per cent increase in the number of health services provided to patients and a 40 per cent increase in staffing numbers compared to previous years. The Albanese Government and the National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation (NACCHO) co-designed Round 3 of the Closing the Gap Major Capital Works Program to fund projects that reflect ACCHO and community priorities. Eligible ACCHOs can visit GrantConnect to apply. Applications close 7 September 2026. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “The Albanese Government is committed to Closing the Gap in health outcomes for First Nations people. “By working in partnership with NACCHO, we are ensuring our funding will go to projects which deliver positive outcomes for First Nations people and communities. “All Australians deserve high-quality health care regardless of where they call home, with this funding to support First Nations health services in urban, regional, rural and remote areas.” Quotes attributable to Minister McCarthy: “Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services provide crucial medical care for First Nations families and are often the only health service available in remote communities. “This funding will help strengthen the Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Sector by supporting upgrades, repairs and new builds. “This is a significant investment designed in partnership with NACCHO, in line with Closing the Gap Priority Reforms.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: “This funding will deliver culturally safe and fit-for-purpose health infrastructure for First Nations people. “The previous two grant rounds demonstrate that this program works. More staff and more services means better health care for First Nations people. “In many remote communities, Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services are the only health service available, making investments like this critical to delivering safe and ongoing care.” Quotes attributable to NACCHO CEO Dr Dawn Casey PSM FAHA: “Health infrastructure is health care. With the right clinic, an ACCHO can expand services, grow its workforce and provide culturally safe care closer to home.” “Round 3 puts $180 million behind the infrastructure priorities ACCHOs have set, from new clinics and extensions to urgent repairs and fit-outs. In eligible rural and remote locations, it will also fund staff housing that helps services recruit and retain health professionals.” “Community-controlled health infrastructure must be shaped by the communities and services that will use it. Priority Reform Two requires exactly that: communities identify what is needed, ACCHOs lead the response and government investment follows." Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health

title: Australia ratifies landmark ocean treaty
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia ratifies landmark ocean treaty Joint media release with: Senator The Hon Murray Watt, Minister for the Environment and Water 24 September 2026 The Albanese Government has formally ratified a landmark international treaty to protect the ocean beyond our country's maritime borders, marking a new era of world ocean conservation. Australia joins more than 90 countries in protecting and sustainably managing the ocean in areas outside national maritime boundaries and exclusive economic zones under the High Seas Biodiversity Treaty (also known as the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction or BBNJ Treaty). Australia was one of the first countries to sign the treaty in 2023. Legislation passed the Parliament this March, allowing it to be formally ratified. The milestone is being celebrated today after Australia's instrument of ratification was deposited overnight during the United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week in New York. Ratification will allow Australia to participate directly in decisions on shared areas. This could include the establishment of new high seas marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments of proposed activities and the sustainable management of shared marine resources – measures never before possible on the high seas. As a Treaty member, Australia will work closely with regional neighbours to prepare the first generation of high seas marine protected area proposals. These will be critical to international efforts to achieve the global target of conserving 30 per cent of the world's ocean by 2030 to support marine biodiversity. Domestically, Australia maintains one of the world's largest representative systems of marine protected areas, covering 52 per cent of our waters. Work is underway to increase the proportion of highly protected marine park zones to at least 30 per cent by 2030. Meanwhile, the Albanese Government has also released Australia's first Sustainable Ocean Plan this week. The Plan provides a national blueprint for ocean stewardship with input from governments and interest groups, addressing key challenges, improving sustainability and supporting the growth of Australia's $229 billion ocean economy. Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs, Penny Wong: "Australia's ocean stewardship is built on the same principles that guide our regional partnerships – respect for international law, shared responsibility, and practical cooperation to tackle challenges no nation can solve alone. "By ratifying this Treaty, Australia can help shape new high seas protections, building on our management of one of the world's largest marine park networks and strengthening the way we safeguard ocean ecosystems. "Healthy oceans keep our economy strong and our food supply secure. They are the lifeblood of a sustainable future for every Australian." Quotes attributable to Minister for the Environment and Water, Murray Watt: "The high seas cover more than half of the planet, yet only around 1 per cent is protected, leaving the ocean open to unsustainable exploitation. "Sustainably managing our ocean at home and on the high seas supports our ocean health, livelihoods, communities, national security and our climate future. "In Australian waters more than half of our maritime jurisdiction is now protected through our marine parks network, including 2.2 million square kilometres in highly protected areas, and that number continues to grow. "But what happens on the high seas has a direct impact on Australia's ocean and the industries that depend on it, such as tourism and fisheries. That's why the Albanese Government is committed to working with other Treaty countries to protect marine areas." Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

title: Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel achieves historic support
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel achieves historic support Media release 24 September 2026 One year after its launch, the Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel has achieved historic support from more than two-thirds of the United Nations. As conflicts become more entrenched and crises worsen, humanitarian personnel face unprecedented threats. In response, Australia led the development of a Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel in partnership with Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia, Japan, Jordan, Sierra Leone, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The Declaration is a shared commitment by 130 countries for stronger accountability, safer access and better protection for humanitarians working in conflict zones. Over the past year, Australia and international partners have been driving concrete and practical action to keep aid workers safe, and putting international pressure on countries that do not comply. To continue building on this momentum, Australia will provide an additional $10 million to strengthen practical protection and accountability measures for frontline humanitarian personnel. Australia is partnering with the UN Department of Safety and Security, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations to deliver security analysis and training for humanitarians, strengthen data and evidence collection to support justice mechanisms, and provide legal and financial assistance for victims and their families. Australia has spearheaded this work in honour of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, and the more than 1,000 humanitarians who have been killed in the last three years while delivering lifesaving support. Humanitarians dedicate their lives to protecting others – this work should never cost them their own. Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

title: Australia to renominate for IMO Council
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia to renominate for IMO Council Joint media release with: The Hon Catherine King MP, Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government 24 September 2026 The Australian Government has marked World Maritime Day by announcing it will seek another two-year term on the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Council. As a founding member of the IMO, Australia has helped shape international maritime standards for almost 75 years. Australia is nominating for re-election to 'Category B' of the IMO Council, which is comprised of states with the largest interest in international seaborne trade. Re-election will allow Australia to continue bringing practical expertise, a consensus-building approach and a regional voice to decisions that shape global maritime safety, environmental protection, international trade and sustainable shipping. Working closely with IMO Member States and industry, Australia is widely recognised for our active leadership on maritime safety, digital maritime services, seafarer welfare, search and rescue and environment protection. Australia is helping shape international responses to some of the maritime sector's most significant challenges, including the transition to low-carbon liquid fuels, the safe adoption of emerging technologies and the prevention of marine pollution. We are also working closely with our Indo-Pacific neighbours, including Small Island Developing States to ensure their needs and concerns are heard, and so we are strengthening maritime capability, resilience, sustainability and safety across the region. Australia's campaign will continue through to the 35th IMO Assembly in December 2027, when Member States will elect Council members for the 2028-29 biennium. Learn more about Australia's candidacy and work at the IMO . Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: "As a middle power, we will continue to support the rules and norms that underpin shared prosperity and shared security. "Our candidacy reflects that commitment, working with partners across all regions to address shared maritime challenges and opportunities. "Through our membership of the IMO Council, Australia strengthens international cooperation and supports global maritime trade, which underpins energy and food security for Australia, the Indo-Pacific, and beyond. "We are proud to work with all IMO Member States and maritime partners toward a safer and more sustainable global maritime system, and look forward to continuing that contribution if re-elected." Quotes attributable to Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government Catherine King: "The vast majority of Australia's imports and exports rely on a strong, safe and sustainable maritime sector. Shipping connects our island nation to global markets, so it's vital we have a seat at the table where international standards are established. "Over decades, Australia has been a reliable and constructive voice on the IMO Council, advocating for maritime safety, environmental protection, seafarer welfare and practical solutions to emerging challenges facing international shipping. "Australia is seeking re-election so we can continue to contribute our expertise to the IMO and collaboratively shape the future of global shipping." title: Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat Joint media release with: The Hon Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia 21 September 2026 At a time of global uncertainty and major challenges, Australia is an untiring advocate for peace and security. We understand that this is best achieved through international cooperation, which is why we are launching our campaign for a seat on the United Nations Security Council, to serve a two-year term from 2029 to 2030. Australia is seeking a seat because a safer world is one governed by rules, not by power and force alone. Our priority is to work across continents and regions to prevent conflict, advance ocean and climate security, and promote peaceful, resilient and inclusive digital futures. The UN Security Council is the world’s principal body for the maintenance of international peace and security. As we know too well, conflicts overseas can affect Australia’s security, economy and way of life. A seat on the Security Council would give Australia a stronger voice in the decisions that affect Australians and our region. As a member of the Security Council, Australia will amplify the views of small and mid-sized states and ensure decisions are informed by a wide range of positions. Australia’s campaign will be guided by a simple approach: listening with respect, partnering as equals and protecting what matters most. As a founding member of the UN and the first President of the Security Council, Australia has been a consistent voice advocating for global peace and security for more than 80 years. If elected, Australia will support bold, practical reform to ensure the UN can continue to fulfil its important mission well into the future. The UN General Assembly will elect 2029-2030 Security Council members in June 2028. Australia last served on the Council in 2013-2014. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: "The hopes of Australians are the hopes of people everywhere – to live in peace and to build a better future. That is the voice that Australia will bring to the security council. “Australia played a pivotal role in the founding of the United Nations – because we have always understood how important it is for small and mid-sized nations to have their voices heard on the challenges facing our world. "Our vision is simple: We listen with respect, we partner as equals and we protect what matters most." Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: “A safer world is one governed by rules, not power and force alone. Australia’s vision is a world where all countries have the freedom to decide their own future. “As an active and ambitious middle power, we have a practical contribution to make to international peace and security. “Australia’s focus on the UN Security Council will be conflict prevention, the protection of civilians and defending the rules that protect us all.” Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

With common history, close geography and shared values, the bonds between our countries, peoples and communities are as diverse as they are deep. Mr Isbister is a senior career officer with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade and was most recently Deputy Secretary, Development, Multilateral and Europe Group. Mr Isbister has over 30 years’ experience working in foreign, humanitarian and development policy. He has served previously as Australia’s Ambassador for the Environment; the Australian Government’s Humanitarian Coordinator; and as Minister Counsellor (Development) in Africa. title: ASEAN-Australia Joint Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers ASEAN-Australia Joint Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia Media releases 17 September 2026 WE, the Member States of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Australia, gathered on the occasion of the ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference (PMC) with Australia on 22 July 2026 in Manila, the Philippines; REAFFIRMING our shared commitment to a peaceful, stable, and prosperous region, and reinforcing an open, transparent, resilient, inclusive, and rules-based regional architecture that upholds international law, with ASEAN at its centre; RECALLING Australia's accession to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) in 2005 and its long-standing support for ASEAN Centrality, the ASEAN-led regional architecture, the ASEAN Charter, and the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP), as ASEAN's first Dialogue Partner and Comprehensive Strategic Partner; RECALLING that the purpose of the TAC is to promote perpetual peace, everlasting amity and cooperation in Southeast Asia, in accordance with the principles of the UN Charter; RECOGNISING that the TAC establishes fundamental principles to govern relations between High Contracting Parties (HCPs), including mutual respect for independence, sovereignty, equality, territorial integrity and national identity of all nations; the right of every State to lead its national existence free from external interference, subversion or coercion; non-interference in the internal affairs of one another; settlement of differences or disputes by peaceful means; renunciation of the threat or use of force; and effective cooperation among Parties; RECOGNISING also that the TAC promotes and serves as a vital framework for close and mutually beneficial cooperation between States to strengthen economic growth and support a peaceful and prosperous region; EMPHASISING that peace and stability in our region are our collective responsibility, and that these principles are as important today as at the time of the TAC's adoption in 1976, and serve as a cornerstone of regional peace and stability as well as a foundational code of conduct for inter-state relations in the region; RECOGNISING that adherence to the TAC creates an enabling environment for peace through norms on the prevention of conflict, management of disputes, and promotion of trust and confidence among States; APPRECIATING the growing relevance and enduring appeal of the Treaty, as reflected in its expansion to an increasing number of HCPs over the past five decades, underscoring its role as a foundation for peaceful relations, mutual respect, and cooperation in the region and beyond; RECALLING our commitment in the ASEAN-Australia Joint Leaders' Statement on Conflict Prevention and Crisis Management in the ASEAN-led Regional Architecture to strengthen cooperation through ASEAN-led mechanisms to promote open communication and dialogue, enhance mutual understanding, respect and benefit, promote strategic trust, and maintain transparent, predictable and responsible conduct in order to reduce the risk of misunderstanding and miscalculation and prevent conflict in the Indo-Pacific region; REAFFIRMING ASEAN Centrality and the central role of the ASEAN-led regional architecture in maintaining international peace, stability, and security as well as in the peaceful resolution of disputes, including full respect for legal and diplomatic processes, without resorting to the threat or use of force, in accordance with international law, including the Charter of the United Nations, the ASEAN Charter, and the TAC; ACKNOWLEDGING that the Indo-Pacific faces an increasingly complex strategic environment marked by heightened geopolitical competition, emerging security challenges, and greater risks of miscalculation and escalation; REAFFIRMING the importance of supporting ASEAN-led efforts in maintaining and promoting peace, stability, maritime safety and security, freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded lawful maritime commerce and other internationally lawful uses of the sea in the region. Emphasising the importance of non-militarisation and the need to enhance mutual trust and confidence, exercise self-restraint in the conduct of activities and avoid actions that may raise the risk of accidents, misunderstanding, and miscalculation and may complicate the situation. Reaffirming the need for States to pursue the peaceful resolutions of disputes, in accordance with universally recognised principles of international law, including the 1982 UNCLOS, and to comply with the relevant Standards and Recommended Practices by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the relevant instruments and conventions of the International Maritime Organization (IMO). We take note of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Statement on Maintaining and Promoting Stability in the Maritime Sphere in Southeast Asia; NOTING the continued relevance of preventive diplomacy, confidence-building measures, and inclusive regional engagement in addressing both traditional and non-traditional security challenges; DO HEREBY AFFIRM TO: UPHOLD the principles and purposes outlined in the TAC as a foundational code of conduct for peaceful relations, mutual respect, cooperation, and stability in the region; STRENGTHEN and utilise ASEAN-led mechanisms, including the ASEAN-Post Ministerial Conference with Australia, East Asia Summit (EAS), ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), and the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus), to advance the principles of the TAC and support peace and security; REITERATE our commitment to preventing and resolving disputes through peaceful means, including full respect for legal and diplomatic processes, without resorting to the threat or use of force, in accordance with international law, including the UN Charter, the 1982 UNCLOS and the TAC; PROMOTE a culture of dialogue, mutual understanding, strategic trust and transparent, predictable, and responsible conduct that reinforces respect for sovereignty and non-interference, while encouraging constructive engagement on shared challenges; SUPPORT the works of ASEAN and relevant ASEAN bodies and entities to develop practical preventive diplomacy, including mechanisms that assess and mitigate risks through exchange of information to facilitate early warning where appropriate and relevant, confidence-building measures, and risk reduction initiatives, to address emerging tensions and help prevent misunderstanding and miscalculation; NOTE the ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Maritime Cooperation and its commitment to intensify maritime cooperation under ASEAN-led mechanisms and initiatives in line with the principles of the ASEAN Charter and the AOIP, including the strengthening of the Expanded ASEAN Maritime Forum (EAMF), the formalisation of the ASEAN Coast Guard Forum (ACF), and the planned establishment of the ASEAN Maritime Centre in the Philippines; ENHANCE cooperation between ASEAN and Australia under the ASEAN-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) to deliver outcomes in areas that contribute to regional stability, including maritime security, economic resilience, supply chain resilience, cyber resilience, countering transnational crime, humanitarian assistance, climate change and disaster management; REAFFIRM commitment to increase and mainstream practical cooperation in the four priority areas of the AOIP, namely maritime cooperation, connectivity, UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030, economic and other possible areas of cooperation, including through ASEAN-led mechanisms like the EAS, in support of the implementation of the ASEAN-Australia Plan of Action (2025-2029) and to further reinforce the ASEAN-Australia CSP; SUPPORT the full implementation of the ASEAN Regional Plan of Action on Women, Peace and Security and the meaningful participation and leadership of women in peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and regional cooperation efforts in advancing objectives and principles of TAC; PROMOTE the Youth, Peace and Security agenda by strengthening the meaningful participation and leadership of youth across all efforts to sustain and advance peace and stability and enhancing their resilience to traditional and emerging threats, including climate, disaster and digital threats; UPHOLD an open, predictable, transparent, inclusive, free, fair, and sustainable rules-based multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organization at its core, ensuring that the multilateral trading system remains, non-discriminatory, and capable of addressing contemporary and emerging challenges, supported by our regional economic architecture, such as the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (RCEP), and the upgraded Agreement Establishing the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA); SUPPORT ASEAN's efforts to promote dialogue, coordination, and cooperation to build regional resilience, including strengthening energy security, financial resilience, and macroeconomic stability; safeguarding food security and agricultural supply chains; strengthening open and rules-based trade, supply chains, and market stability; and strengthening people-centred and humanitarian response; COMMIT TO strengthening Southeast Asia's energy security by accelerating the clean energy transition, including through support for the ASEAN Power Grid; cooperation to strengthen energy policy, planning and management; support for the development of clean energy supply chains and infrastructure; and the mobilisation of finance for renewable energy projects; SUPPORT ASEAN's efforts to revitalise the ARF, to enhance its effectiveness, relevance, and function as the leading regional security forum and to promote confidence-building measures and preventive diplomacy, as well as to support its capacity to address emerging political and security challenges; SUPPORT ASEAN's ongoing efforts to enhance the TAC's relevance and visibility in the region and beyond, including by working together towards the successful adoption of an ASEAN-sponsored resolution to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the TAC during the 80th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, and aligning external engagements with the Guidelines on the Modalities for Engagement with HCPs under the TAC; PROMOTE the operationalisation of the Guidelines on the Modalities for Engagement of ASEAN with HCPs under the TAC, adopted by the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, which established modalities of engagement aimed at deepening cooperation with HCPs, especially those that do not yet maintain formal partnerships with ASEAN; UTILISE the principles espoused in the TAC to guide responses to contemporary challenges, including geopolitical and geostrategic shifts, emerging technologies, and non-traditional security threats, and contribute to an enabling environment for sustainable development, economic cooperation, and shared prosperity; COMMIT TO working together, in partnership and solidarity, to ensure the TAC continues to serve as a guiding framework for regional relations and as a foundation for preventing conflict and fostering enduring peace. title: Australia deploys drone specialists as part of expanded Nepal response
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia deploys drone specialists as part of expanded Nepal response Joint media release with: The Hon Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister for International Development The Hon Kristy McBain MP, Minister for Regional Development, Local Government and Territories 03 September 2026 Australia will deploy a team of specialist drone operators to contribute to Nepal’s search and rescue effort and boost our humanitarian support package following the catastrophic floods. The team, including members of Fire and Rescue New South Wales and the Queensland Fire Department, will depart in the coming days as part of a 15-person Disaster Assistance Response Team. They will use advanced drone technology to provide rapid mapping and imaging to support Nepali authorities' search operations. In response to Australia’s ongoing offers of assistance, the Government of Nepal has now requested this support. We stand ready to provide further search, rescue and recovery assistance. The latest deployment is in addition to the 19 Australian personnel already dispatched to Nepal to support the crisis response, including consular and humanitarian officers, Australian Federal Police and Defence personnel. 38 Australians remain unaccounted for. Australian officials are working closely with authorities in Nepal and China to support efforts to establish their whereabouts and provide assistance to their families. The conditions facing search and recovery teams remain extremely challenging. Communications are difficult, infrastructure has been destroyed and many areas are still difficult to reach. Australians have responded to the disaster in Nepal with extraordinary generosity, with over $4 million donated to the Emergency Action Alliance that is providing critical support for recovery efforts. In response, the Australian Government will provide a further $3 million to match public donations. This contribution will enable the delivery of vital shelter, water, sanitation and healthcare, as well as providing children with desperately needed temporary learning spaces. It brings the Australian Government’s ongoing humanitarian support package to a total of $11 million. Australians wishing to donate can visit emergencyaction.org.au . Our thoughts remain with all those waiting for news of family and friends, and with the search and rescue teams working in extraordinarily difficult circumstances. The Australian Government continues to do everything we can to confirm the welfare of those who remain unaccounted for and support their families and loved ones. text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Landmark six-nation partnership delivers East Micronesia Cable Joint media release with: Pat Conroy MP, Minister for Pacific Island Affairs, Minister for Defence Industry 01 September 2026 A landmark six-nation partnership backed by the Albanese Government has delivered the East Micronesia Cable system, bringing reliable, high-capacity telecommunications connectivity to communities across Micronesia for the first time. The 2,250 km East Micronesia Cable will bring faster, more reliable and more affordable internet to over 100,000 people across Naoero, Tarawa in Kiribati and Kosrae in the Federated States of Micronesia. This will provide the regional connectivity that underpins essential services, economic activity and community relationships. The cable also greatly reduces the risk of telecommunications outages, helping people and businesses stay connected to the everyday services they rely on. The Australian Government contributed approximately $AUD65 million to the $AUD135 million project through the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific. Bringing together the Federated States of Micronesia, Kiribati and Naoero, with support from Australia, Japan and the United States, the project demonstrates what can be achieved when Pacific countries and partners work together to deliver shared regional priorities. With the East Micronesia Cable complete, all Pacific Islands Forum members are now connected to undersea telecommunications infrastructure for the first time, a milestone supporting a more connected and digitally resilient Blue Pacific. Quotes attributable to Foreign Minister Penny Wong: "Improved connectivity enhances the Pacific region's resilience and capacity to respond to economic and security challenges. "The East Micronesia Cable will drive growth and opportunity, strengthen essential services and contribute to long-term regional stability, which benefits us all." Quotes attributable to Pacific Island Affairs Minister Pat Conroy: "The East Micronesia Cable demonstrates what can be achieved when Pacific nations work together for the benefit of the region. "Together with the Pacific and partners Japan and the United States, we are delivering lasting infrastructure that builds a safe, peaceful and prosperous region and will benefit Pacific communities for decades to come. "The East Micronesia Cable will help families stay connected, support businesses to grow, expand access to education and healthcare and create new opportunities in an increasingly digital world." The signing of the ANZUS Treaty in 1951 formalised the Australia-US Alliance, which was forged on the battlefields of two world wars. For more than seven decades, the Alliance has underpinned peace, stability and prosperity in our region and continues to contribute to the region’s strategic balance. Today the United States remains our closest ally and principal strategic partner. As we look to the future, we work closely with the United States to deliver for the Australian and American people, deepening the bonds of friendship and goodwill that have connected our nations for generations. The Alliance between Australia and New Zealand remains closer than ever, tightly bound by our shared history. Our security partnership was founded in the days of the first ANZACs, with this spirit continuing to enliven our modern Alliance. Today, our Alliance continues to evolve, including efforts to operate as an increasingly integrated, combat capable ANZAC force. Our Alliance has a critical role in safeguarding national security and supporting stability in the Indo-Pacific as we work to shape a region where sovereignty is respected. As we mark this milestone amidst an increasingly complex strategic environment, we reaffirm the enduring value of ANZUS. title: Australia’s response to Nepal-China floods
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia’s response to Nepal-China floods Joint media release with: The Hon Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister for International Development 28 August 2026 The Australian Government is rapidly mobilising consular and humanitarian support in response to the catastrophic floods along the Nepal-China border, including through a $5 million assistance package for affected communities. We understand at least 39 Australians are among those reported missing. Australian officials are working urgently to confirm their welfare and provide assistance to those affected. The extraordinary scale of this disaster and the remoteness of the affected region mean immense challenges lie ahead for the response and recovery. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade is deploying additional personnel to support Australians affected by the disaster. In addition to the staff at the Australian Embassy in Nepal, a Crisis Response Team (CRT) member and a Regional Consular Officer have been deployed and are on the ground in Kathmandu. Further regional and CRT surge support are being prepared for deployment. The Government will send an initial team of three humanitarian response specialists within the next 48 hours to help Australian staff already on the ground. Drawn from the Australia Assists program, the Rapid Response Team has expertise in humanitarian assessment, logistics, communications and planning. As part of the response, the Australian Government will provide $5 million in humanitarian assistance to support urgent disaster response and recovery efforts. The funding will be delivered through established partners to provide support such as food, emergency shelter, clean water and sanitation. These floods have devastated communities along both sides of the border, sweeping away villages, damaging critical infrastructure, and leaving thousands displaced. With roads and bridges destroyed, many communities remain isolated and difficult to reach, underscoring the need for rapid humanitarian assistance. Australia’s assistance includes: $2 million to the World Food Programme, which has already dispatched food rations and provided logistics support for Nepal’s emergency response. $2 million to Australian NGOs through the Australian Humanitarian Partnership to provide support such as emergency shelter, hygiene kits, blankets, medical support and psychosocial support. $1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance to support locally-led recovery and rehabilitation efforts in affected areas. Australians wishing to donate should visit the Emergency Action Alliance webpage . Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

Under the Jakarta Treaty signed in February this year, the Australia-Indonesia Institute will receive $11.4 million to expand its cultural exchange and grants programs over 4 years, creating more opportunities for Australians and Indonesians to learn from each other and strengthen ties. title: Australia–Indonesia Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Meeting
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia–Indonesia Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Meeting Joint media release The Hon Richard Marles MP, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Defence 26 August 2026 Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles and Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong will today welcome Indonesian Defense Minister Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin and Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono to Melbourne. At the 10th Australia–Indonesia Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Meeting, Ministers will discuss cooperation on defence, security, economic and development priorities. Australia and Indonesia share a deep and longstanding partnership, underpinned by trust, mutual respect and close cooperation. The meeting follows Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and President Prabowo Subianto’s signing in February of the landmark Australia–Indonesia Treaty on Common Security (the Jakarta Treaty ), which strengthens defence cooperation and increases consultation and cooperation on shared security challenges. Quotes attributable to Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles: “Our relationship with Indonesia continues to go from strength to strength, reflecting mutual trust and a shared commitment to regional stability. “I look forward to our meeting where we will have the opportunity to discuss progress across a range of practical defence and security initiatives to operationalise the Australia-Indonesia Defence Cooperation Agreement and the Jakarta Treaty .” Quotes attributable to Foreign Minister Penny Wong: “This is our first meeting since the signing of the Jakarta Treaty and marks a new chapter in the relationship between Australia and Indonesia. “Together we are building on the strong ties between our countries and deepening cooperation across the full breadth of our partnership.” Media note: access to imagery/vision will be available at: Defence Imagery DFAT Media Library Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

title: Centre for Australia-India Relations board appointments

I am pleased to appoint: Mr Robin Khuda - Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Airtrunk Mr Faz Pollard - Director of Adarsh Australia Professor Veena Sahajwalla AO - Director of the Centre for Sustainable Materials Research and Technology at the University of New South Wales I am pleased to reappoint four incumbent members to the Advisory Board: Ms Amrit Gill - Chief Executive Officer of Theatre Network Australia Ms Catriona Jackson - Former CEO of Universities Australia Ms Mitu Bhowmick Lange AM - Founder and Director of Mind-Blowing Films Mr Amit Singh - Managing Partner of Mandala Partners Advisory Board Chair Ms Swati Dave, Dr Helen Nugent AC, Mr Steve Waugh AO and Secretary Jan Adams AO PSM will also continue their current terms on the Board. The Centre works across government, industry, academia, and the community to build greater understanding of the Australia-India relationship and encourage business to seize economic opportunities. Each member was chosen for their expertise in specific areas of interest to the Australia-India economic relationship and brings with them rich experience in their relevant sectors. The Advisory Board helps set the strategic priorities for the Centre’s programs and activities, supporting partnerships in business, the arts, education, health, science, technology, and sport. The appointments come at a time of great momentum in Australia-India relations, following Prime Minister Modi’s recent visit to Melbourne and the ongoing work under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to strengthen collaboration between our two nations. I thank outgoing Advisory Board members Ms Florence Drummond, Mr Gunjan Pagare, the Hon Martin Hamilton-Smith and Mr Sameer Kumar for their service to the Centre and the Australia-India relationship. title: Stronger safeguards for Foreign Arrangements
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Stronger safeguards for Foreign Arrangements Joint media release with: The Hon Matt Thistlethwaite MP, Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade 20 August 2026 The Albanese Government has strengthened and streamlined Australia’s Foreign Arrangements Scheme, with legislation passing the Parliament today to help ensure arrangements are consistent with Australia’s national interest. The reforms modernise the Scheme, which provides Commonwealth oversight of arrangements entered into by states, territories, local governments and public universities with foreign entities. The changes more clearly embed the national interest in legislation, improve risk management, and streamline notification requirements. They also capture evolving forms of international engagement, such as arrangements involving overseas campuses of Australian universities. The reforms implement the recommendations from the 2025 independent review of the Scheme led by Rosemary Huxtable AO PSM. The Government recognises concerns regarding researcher-to-researcher collaboration and will require universities to have appropriate policies and processes in place to identify, monitor and manage associated risks. For the first time, universities will be legally required to assess whether research projects could adversely affect the national interest or be inconsistent with Australia’s foreign policy. The Albanese Government has been consistently clear that universities must play their role in managing risks and this reform will help ensure they do so. Australia is strongly committed to international education and research cooperation that is consistent with our foreign policy. These reforms will help keep Australia open to the world while appropriately managing risk and protecting our national interest. title: Deepening Australia and Vietnam's economic partnership
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Deepening Australia and Vietnam's economic partnership Joint media release with: The Hon Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia Senator the Hon Don Farrell, Minister For Trade And Tourism The Hon Catherine King MP, Minister For Transport, Infrastructure, Regional Development And Local Government The Hon Jason Clare MP, Minister For Education The Hon Julie Collins MP, Minister For Agriculture, Fisheries And Forestry 11 August 2026 Australia and Vietnam have agreed to strengthen cooperation across education, trade and innovation, to enhance the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam and President of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, His Excellency Mr To Lam issued a Joint Statement on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between Australia and Vietnam on priorities including economic engagement, climate, energy and science. The two leaders also issued a Joint Statement on Economic Resilience Cooperation and a Joint Statement on Science, Research and Innovation. The agreements announced today will strengthen economic ties and create new opportunities for businesses in both countries. Trade Ministers signed an agreement to deepen cooperation in the digital economy, including supporting cross-border trade to promote e-commerce and create opportunities for Australian businesses in digital health and banking services. The visit also saw Vietjet announce yesterday direct flights between Ho Chi Minh City and Western Sydney International Airport. Flights will begin in January 2027, operating twice a week before increasing to three services a week from March. Australia and Vietnam also agreed to continue to strengthen existing cooperation on agriculture and sustainable development, including biosecurity, food safety and aquaculture. Australia secured agreement for the recommencement of market access for Australian game meat, including kangaroo meat. Both countries are working toward closer health cooperation, which will see Australia supporting medical research, pandemic preparedness, and rural and remote healthcare in Vietnam. Education remains one of the strongest links between Australia and Vietnam. A new Memorandum of Understanding on vocational education and training will support Australian providers to deliver industry-focused training in Vietnam. Australia also welcomed Vietnam's approval of an investment licence for RMIT University, allowing it to establish a new campus in Hanoi. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: "I am very pleased to welcome General Secretary and President To Lam to Australia. "Vietnam is one of Australia's closest partners in our region and our relationship continues to go from strength to strength. "Today's agreements will make it easier to do business, create new opportunities for trade and investment, strengthen education and research links, and bring our countries even closer together. "More flights, more trade and stronger education links are good for Australian jobs, Australian businesses and our economy." Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: "Our economic partnership with Vietnam contributes not only to the prosperity of our two countries, but to a stronger and more resilient region. "By deepening trade and investment links, we are helping build shared prosperity in an increasingly uncertain world." Quotes attributable to Minister for Trade and Tourism Don Farrell: "The Albanese Labor Government is committed to deepening our engagement with Vietnam by delivering practical outcomes for our people, our businesses and our region. "Vietnam is experiencing rapid economic growth with an expanding middle class, and we're ensuring Australia's world class producers and exporters are best placed to meet the country's growing demand. "The new flights from Vietnam to Western Sydney are a huge win for tourists and businesses who will now have greater choice and increased opportunities between our two nations." Quotes attributable to the Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government Catherine King: "Vietjet's flights into Western Sydney International Airport will be a real boost for tourism and business in Sydney's west, as well as for Western Sydney families looking for a holiday escape. "Welcoming our fifth airline is an exciting update, as we work towards passenger flights commencing on Sunday the 25th of October." Quotes attributable to Minister for Education Jason Clare: "Education is one of the most important bridges between Australia and Vietnam. "It's not just about Vietnamese students studying in Australia, it's also about Australian universities like RMIT taking the best of Australian education to Vietnam. "These connections build the skills our countries need and the friendships that bring us closer together." Quotes attributable to Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry Julie Collins: "Australia is a trusted and reliable supplier of agricultural, fisheries and forestry products to Vietnam because of our well-earned reputation for providing high quality, safe and sustainably produced goods. "This agreement demonstrates the strength of our relationship with Vietnam, and it is wonderful to see cooperation like this also result in progress on long-standing market-access requests that will expand opportunities for Australian farmers and producers to showcase our world-class products on the international stage. "Our Government will continue working tirelessly to expand opportunities for our farmers and producers." Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam and President of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, His Excellency Mr To Lam issued the Joint Statement on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between Australia and Vietnam, reinforcing cooperation on shared priorities including defence and security. As part of the visit, the two countries announced new practical measures to strengthen defence and security cooperation. Australia and Vietnam's Ministers for Defence agreed to an updated Joint Vision Statement on Defence Cooperation to support closer exchanges, including across maritime security and disaster relief. Australian and Vietnamese defence forces will work more closely together, including by sharing expertise on search and rescue operations and participating in joint training. Respective border agencies signed memoranda of understanding for further work together to combat transnational crime, strengthen border protection and enhance maritime cooperation. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: "Australia and Vietnam are close partners and we are both committed to a peaceful, stable and prosperous region. "These new agreements deliver practical cooperation between our countries and help ensure we can meet the challenges of an increasingly complex strategic environment." Quotes attributable to Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles: "Vietnam is an important defence partner for Australia, and we are committed to deepening cooperation in ways that directly contribute to the stability and security of our region. "By expanding practical cooperation across areas such as maritime security, search and rescue, disaster relief and training, we are building stronger capabilities and closer ties between our two defence forces." Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: "Australia and Vietnam are strengthening our defence and security ties as result of the growing strategic trust under our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. "We both share a commitment to a region where countries can make their own decisions, sovereignty is respected, and disputes can be managed peacefully." Quotes attributable to Minister for Home Affairs Tony Burke: "The threats we're facing today do not stop at national borders. If cyber criminals and organised crime gangs are going to function on a transnational basis, then our response needs to be transnational as well. "One country alone can't deal with these growing threats. Strong cooperation with trusted partners is essential to keep our communities safe." Enhance preparedness for respiratory disease outbreaks using AI-driven forecasting of health and economic impacts. Advance Australia-UAE marine conservation efforts through collaborative research, technology innovation, and expert exchange. Build animal disease surveillance and response capability in Oman with specialised epidemiology training for veterinarians. Together, these projects showcase Australian expertise and deliver practical opportunities for collaboration and skills exchange. I congratulate this year's recipients. Their projects reflect the innovation and ambition that continues to shape Australia's international engagement and create new opportunities for trade and investment. Over the past decade, the CAAR Grants Program has invested more than $2.3 million in initiatives that strengthen ties between Australia and the Middle East and North Africa. title: All Pacific Islands Forum members now connected by undersea cables
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers All Pacific Islands Forum members now connected by undersea cables Joint media release with: Pat Conroy MP, Minister for Pacific Island Affairs 07 August 2026 Australia has helped achieve a major milestone for the region, with all Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) members now connected to undersea telecommunications cables for the first time. Working alongside Pacific governments and development partners, Australia has helped deliver more than 10,300 kilometres of new undersea cables, ensuring every PIF member is connected to the global cable network. A more connected Pacific advances our shared interests by strengthening regional resilience, supporting economic development and deepening connections between our countries and peoples. Australia has committed more than $500 million since 2018 to support undersea cable connectivity across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. This investment has helped deliver cable projects across nine countries, including primary cable connections for Naoero, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tuvalu, Tarawa in Kiribati, and Kosrae in the Federated States of Micronesia. Australia is also working with partners to strengthen the reliability and resilience of telecommunications infrastructure through support for second international cable connections in Tonga, Papua New Guinea, Palau and Solomon Islands. These investments are being delivered in partnership with Japan, New Zealand, and the United States, as well as Taiwan. They will help connect Pacific governments, businesses, communities and peoples to global networks and digital markets, opening new opportunities for trade, investment, innovation and economic participation. Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs, Senator Penny Wong: "For the first time, every Pacific Islands Forum member now has access to the digital infrastructure needed to participate fully in the modern economy, backed in with Australian support. "A more connected Pacific is a more resilient Pacific. This infrastructure strengthens economic growth, supports essential services and will help underpin a more peaceful, stable and prosperous region." Quotes attributable to Minister for Pacific Island Affairs, Pat Conroy MP: "Faster, more affordable and more reliable digital services will help integrate our economies, making it easier for Pacific peoples and businesses to connect, and investment to flow across the region. "With new connections comes greater opportunities, better information flows and knowledge sharing, supporting Pacific Island countries to fully participate in the global economy." At a time of global uncertainty, it is more important than ever that Pacific countries work together to advance our shared interests, uphold Pacific priorities and strengthen the peace, stability and prosperity of our region. By bringing together its 18 members, the PIF makes us stronger and more resilient. The meeting will help prepare for the PIF Leaders Meeting in Palau next month and provide an opportunity to advance discussions on the region's key priorities, including peace and security, climate change, and economic development. The visit comes a month after Australia and Fiji signed two historic treaties in Suva – the Vuvale Union and Ocean of Peace Alliance – that will deepen our bilateral relationship and contribute to our countries’ prosperity, security and resilience for decades to come. They are also the first treaties to implement the Ocean of Peace Declaration, endorsed by Pacific leaders in 2025, with regionalism at the heart of both agreements. As a founding member of the PIF, Australia is a partner the region can count on. Australia strongly supports the PIF’s role in bringing countries together and advancing our shared vision of a region where nations can make their own choices and shape their own futures. title: Australia provides firefighting support to France
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia provides firefighting support to France Joint media release with: The Hon Richard Marles MP, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Defence The Hon Kristy McBain MP, Minister for Emergency Management The Hon Jihad Dib MP, NSW Minister for Emergency Services 31 July 2026 Australia is sending aerial firefighting assets and teams to support the response to devastating wildfires in France. A CH-47D Chinook helicopter, equipped with an 11,300-litre water tank, and a Bell 412 reconnaissance and support aircraft will be deployed to France, accompanied by 24 highly skilled aerial and ground crew from the New South Wales Rural Fire Service (NSW RFS). Together, they will support around-the-clock firefighting operations, providing much-needed relief to emergency services responding on the ground. The wildfires in France are among the worst the country has experienced in decades, driven by multiple active fire fronts and a prolonged summer heatwave. The NSW RFS is internationally recognised as an expert in bushfire management and represents the very best of Australian emergency management capability. The assistance is being provided in response to a request from the French Government. It will be delivered in close partnership with the Australian Defence Force, which will support the rapid deployment of personnel, aircraft and equipment through strategic airlift and logistics. The deployment will take place in coming days. Quotes attributable to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles: “Australia and France work closely together in our region, and we are proud to be supporting them now during their time of need. “The Australian Defence Force will make an important contribution to these efforts, using its assets to help get assistance to where it’s needed.” Quotes attributable to the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Senator Penny Wong: “France is a close and valued friend of Australia, and we stand with the French people as they respond to these devastating wildfires.” “The scale of these fires is immense, and it is in moments like these that the strength of our partnership and solidarity is most evident.” Quotes attributable to the Minister for Emergency Management, Kristy McBain: “Having seen firsthand the severe impacts bushfires have had on both my own community and many others across Australia, my heart goes out to the people of France. “Australia has some of the finest fire-fighting capability on the planet and we are only too happy to do whatever we can to assist, just as France came to our aid during the 2019-2020 Black Summer Bushfires. “I want to thank the emergency services personnel who are travelling to France. I wish you a safe deployment.” Quotes attributable to the NSW Minister for Emergency Services, Jihad Dib: “Our emergency services are proud to support our international partners in their time of need, and the Chinook will be a welcome boost to French firefighting capabilities with its large water storage and night-time capabilities.” “The deployment of RFS personnel, the Chinook and Bell 412 support aircraft, together with the ongoing work of the Marie Bashir large air tanker in the US, demonstrates the depth of capability NSW can deliver during major fire emergencies.” Vision of the assets can be accessed via Dropbox . title: Australia and Singapore sign landmark Protocol on Economic Resilience and Essential Supplies
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia and Singapore sign landmark Protocol on Economic Resilience and Essential Supplies Joint media release with: Richard Marles MP, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Defence Senator Don Farrell, Minister for Trade and Tourism 27 July 2026 Australia and Singapore have signed a new Protocol on Economic Resilience and Essential Supplies under the Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement, strengthening cooperation on energy security, critical supply chains and trade. The Agreement delivers on the commitment made by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on 10 April 2026 to bolster the security of essential supplies, including petrol, and to keep trade flowing during periods of disruption. Singapore is Australia's largest fuel supplier, providing 55 per cent of Australia's petrol, 15 per cent of its diesel and 23 per cent of its aviation fuel. With Australia importing around 90 per cent of its fuel needs, the agreement will support both countries' economic resilience. The Protocol also establishes the Australia-Singapore Economic Resilience Dialogue, creating a dedicated mechanism to advance practical cooperation on shared challenges. The Agreement was signed at the Singapore-Australia Joint Ministerial Committee (SAJMC) hosted in Adelaide today by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles, Minister for Foreign Affairs, Penny Wong, and Minister for Trade and Tourism, Don Farrell. Marking 30 years of cooperation, the SAJMC was first established in 1996 by then Prime Ministers Keating and Goh Chok Tong. Today's discussions demonstrate the tangible value of Australia's relationship with Singapore, a trusted regional partner with whom we work closely to advance our shared prosperity and security. The SAJMC follows a series of high-level engagements in recent months, including the conclusion of negotiations on the Protocol by Minister Wong and Minister Farrell in April, and the 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue in May attended by the Deputy Prime Minister Marles. Today, Ministers also agreed to further enhance our defence ties, witnessing the signing of the Australia-Singapore Industrial Base Resiliency Arrangement. This agreement builds on the enhanced Memorandum of Understanding on defence cooperation announced in October 2025, by strengthening cooperation between our defence industries and improving the resilience of our supply chains. More information on the Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement is available on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade website. Quote attributable to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles: “Australia’s long-standing friendship and partnership with Singapore is underscored by a deep strategic trust.” “Our militaries have a long history of working together in our region, in support of the security and resilience of the Indo-Pacific.” “Today we are growing our already strong defence partnership even further by strengthening cooperation between our defence forces and our defence industries.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: “Australia and Singapore have built one of the region's closest and most trusted partnerships, underpinned by practical cooperation across trade, defence, energy security and economic resilience.” “At a time of increasing global uncertainty, the Protocol will help ensure Australia and Singapore can respond together to disruptions and maintain access to the supplies our economies depend on.” “Australia and Singapore's prosperity and security are closely linked. Together, we remain committed to strengthening the rules and institutions that support an open, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Trade and Tourism Don Farrell: “Singapore is one of Australia's closest trade and investment partners.” “The signing of this Protocol is an important step to ensure Australia has what it needs to keep moving in the face of global supply chain disruptions.” “The Protocol builds on the success of our free trade agreement and reinforces both countries' support for open, free and fair trade.” Media enquiries Minister's office: (02) 6277 7500 DFAT Media Liaison: (02) 6261 1555

title: Middle East travel advice
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Middle East travel advice Joint media release with: The Hon Matt Thistlethwaite MP, Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade 24 July 2026 The Australian Government has raised the travel advice level for Bahrain and Kuwait due to the deteriorating security situation in the Middle East. Travel advice for both countries has been raised to Level 4, ‘Do not travel’. Bahrain and Kuwait now join Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Palestine, Syria and Yemen as ‘Do not travel’ destinations. The situation in the Middle East remains unpredictable. Military strikes are intensifying in a number of locations in the region. There is a risk of further escalation. Australians in ‘Do not travel’ countries should consider leaving if safe to do so and while commercial flights remain available. Travel advice for the remaining countries in the Middle East region is set at Level 3, ‘Reconsider your need to travel’. This includes Saudi Arabia, Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Jordan. We understand many Australians continue to travel through major transit hubs in the region in order to get to other destinations. We urge Australians with travel plans through Level 3 countries to strongly consider whether their plans are essential. Airspace may close at short notice. Flights can be cancelled with little warning. Borders can close. Phone and internet access may be disrupted. You could become stranded for extended periods. Smartraveller keeps all travel advice under constant review and levels could change at short notice. Australians in the region and those looking to travel should subscribe to Smartraveller.gov.au to keep up to date. Australians in need of emergency consular assistance should contact DFAT’s 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre on 1300 555 135, or +61 2 6261 3305 (if calling from overseas).
