title: National Accounts – March quarter 2026
text: National Accounts – March quarter 2026 3 June 2026 National Accounts – March quarter 2026 Today’s National Accounts show the Australian economy grew 0.3 per cent in the March quarter, to be 2.5 per cent higher through the year. This is very solid in the circumstances. This is the equal fastest pace of annual growth in almost three years. It shows how resilient our economy is at a time of substantial global economic volatility. The biggest takeaway of today’s National Accounts is that all of the growth in the March quarter came from the private sector. Private sector investment is booming in Australia. Economic growth was driven by strong growth in business investment, solid consumption and ongoing growth in dwelling investment. New public final demand made almost no contribution to quarterly GDP growth. Annual growth in Australia is faster than almost every major advanced economy and above the OECD average. The Australian economy is outperforming when it comes to annual growth, has stronger employment growth than almost every major advanced economy, and has lower gross debt‑to‑GDP than every single major advanced economy. Australia is not immune from the volatility and uncertainty in the global economy, but these new numbers show we are well placed and well prepared to confront these challenges. The largest and most significant contributor to growth in today’s figures was business investment, which recorded its fastest quarterly growth in nearly a decade and a half. New business investment grew 5.7 per cent in the quarter to be 10.4 per cent higher through the year. It contributed 0.7 percentage points to quarterly growth. Business investment was driven by the largest through‑the‑year rise in machinery and equipment investment in more than two decades. While data centre investment has been strong, business investment has also been supported by the rollout of renewable energy and battery storage. The outlook for investment is encouraging, with CAPEX survey data from last week showing the level of nominal spending was upgraded in both 2025–26 and 2026–27 to around $200 billion in each year. CAPEX was more than six times higher than the median market expectation for the quarter. As a share of the economy, business investment is now at 12.9 per cent, the highest in nearly a decade and much higher than the 11.3 per cent we inherited. Business investment collapsed under our predecessors but we’re turning that around. Annualised average new business investment is growing at 5.2 per cent under us after going backwards by an average of 1.3 per cent under them. Business investment was the key reason why private demand grew faster than public demand in the quarter. New private final demand grew 1.3 per cent, to be 4.0 per cent higher through the year. It contributed 0.9 percentage points to growth this quarter, which is the sixth consecutive quarter that new private final demand has contributed more to growth than public demand. There was continued strength in dwelling investment, which for the first time in eleven years recorded its ninth consecutive quarter of growth. Dwelling investment grew 0.7 per cent in the quarter to be 3.5 per cent higher through the year. When we came to office, it was going backwards by 3.6 per cent. This comes after data yesterday which showed trend building approvals grew 9.8 per cent in the 12 months to April. This is another solid turnaround from the fall of 21.6 per cent when we came to office. These figures are welcome, especially given our continued primary focus on boosting housing supply to improve affordability and homeownership. Household consumption grew 0.5 per cent in the quarter to be 2.5 per cent higher through the year. The data shows that households in particular were not immune from the impacts of the conflict, with elevated fuel prices contributing to operation of vehicles experiencing the largest price increase across all consumption categories, rising 1.8 per cent. The data also showed that mortgage interest costs were up 5.1 per cent in the quarter, but the full impact of recent interest rate movements will be reflected in future quarters. Despite these impacts, solid consumption was supported by a resilient labour market in this quarter. Compensation of employees was up 1.2 per cent in the quarter to be 5.9 per cent higher through the year. This has again pushed the wage share of income to 54.2 per cent, up from the 49.0 per cent we inherited. In annual terms, the National Accounts measure of prices moderated to 3.0 per cent, down from 3.2 per cent in the previous quarter. As with recent CPI figures, these price increases remain higher than we would like but it is still welcome to see them ease in the quarter. Public final demand made almost no contribution to growth in the quarter. It grew 0.1 per cent, to be 2.5 per cent higher through the year. This is a significant moderation from 0.9 per cent in the previous quarter. The weakness in public final demand was partially driven by the Government’s responsible decision to end energy bill relief, which saw government consumption fall by 0.2 per cent in the quarter. Net exports detracted 0.8 percentage points from growth. Exports fell 1.1 per cent in the quarter, as exports for iron ore and coal were impacted by weather events. Imports grew by 2.1 per cent in the quarter largely reflecting the strong business investment. Productivity declined in the quarter but increased 0.3 per cent through the year. While quarterly productivity figures can be volatile, we are doing more in the Budget to turn Australia’s longstanding productivity challenge around. The pickup in the private economy, driven by booming investment, is an important strength as we confront a challenging global economic environment. Under Labor, annual economic growth is ahead of every major advanced economy, business investment is strengthening, more than 1.2 million jobs have been created, unemployment is low, participation is at near record highs and wages growth is solid. The Budget we handed down last month was all about cutting taxes for workers, making it easier to get into the housing market, and boosting productivity. The Budget included $3.5 billion in business tax relief to encourage even more investment and innovation in the private sector. This Government and our Budget is very focused on resilience and reform, to respond to our economic challenges and make the most of our opportunities at a time of substantial volatility and uncertainty in the world. There will always be those who want to talk our economy and our people down for political purposes, but these National Accounts are a very welcome and timely reminder of our strengths in challenging times. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: More tax cuts in one month from today
text: More tax cuts in one month from today 1 June 2026 More tax cuts in one month from today The Albanese Labor Government is delivering another tax cut for every Australian taxpayer in one month from today. We’re putting more money back into millions of Australians’ pockets. From 1 July, over 14 million Australians will get another tax cut of up to $268. This is on top of the tax relief we’ve already delivered since coming to government. This is the next step in our plan to reduce the average worker’s income tax by up to $2,816 a year from 2027–28. In every state and territory, more people will receive Labor’s tax cut from next month: Around 4.4 million taxpayers in New South Wales Around 3.7 million taxpayers in Victoria Around 2.9 million taxpayers in Queensland Around 1.6 million taxpayers in Western Australia Around 1 million taxpayers in South Australia Around 300,000 taxpayers in Tasmania Around 300,000 taxpayers in the ACT And around 130,000 taxpayers in the Northern Territory Younger Australians make up the largest share of those who benefit, with over eight million Gen Z and Millennial taxpayers receiving a tax cut – roughly 60 per cent of all recipients. Lower income taxes are central to our economic plan, which is all about providing immediate cost of living relief while also addressing longer‑term challenges. The Budget handed down last month included a new Working Australians Tax Offset of up to $250 from the 2027–28 tax year. We are also introducing a new $1,000 instant tax deduction for the 2026–27 year. It means we are cutting taxes five times, in three different ways: A new tax cut on 1 July 2026 Another tax cut on 1 July 2027 Our existing Cost of Living Tax Cuts that took effect in 2024 The $250 Working Australians Tax Offset The $1,000 instant tax deduction Together, these tax cuts will mean the average worker benefits by up to $2,816, compared to 2023–24 tax settings. The Coalition voted against the new tax cuts coming in next month and next year. If the Liberals and Nationals had won the last election, income taxes would be higher from 1 July this year and higher on 1 July next year. They have also been clear that they plan to vote against our $250 Working Australians Tax Offset and $1,000 instant tax deduction which are currently before the Parliament. Labor is getting on with the job of cutting income taxes and making the tax system better and fairer. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Business investment booming under Labor
text: Business investment booming under Labor 28 May 2026 Business investment booming under Labor New figures released by the ABS today show private sector investment is soaring under the Albanese Labor Government. Capital expenditure has far exceeded market expectations, with billions more being poured into productive investments. This is good news for Australian businesses and good news for our economy. New private capital expenditure (capex) grew very strongly at 6.5 per cent in the March quarter – more than six times the median market expectation. It means capex is up 14.6 per cent through the year. Data centres, renewable energy and battery storage drove non‑mining capex, which grew 8.8 per cent through the quarter and is up 20.9 per cent through the year. These kinds of infrastructure projects are a priority for our government, and clearly, they’re a priority for the private sector as well. We know capex can be lumpy, but these very welcome figures come despite the economic uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East. Even before these numbers, business investment was growing by an average of 3.9 per cent under this Labor Government after going backwards 1.3 per cent under the Coalition. These figures once again show we’re well placed and well prepared to confront this global uncertainty and volatility, with faster growth than any major advanced economy at the end of last year, low unemployment, solid wages growth and stronger public finances. This is another important reminder that some people should stop talking our economy down. In our most recent Budget, the Albanese Government announced $3.5 billion in business tax relief measures to encourage more private investment. This includes making the small business instant asset write‑off permanent, introducing two‑year loss carry back for companies with turnover of up to $1 billion, introducing loss refundability and expanding incentives for venture capital. These measures are all about giving businesses the confidence to invest and will support a more productive and resilient economy. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Joint media release: Australia backs stronger coastlines and communities in the Pacific
text: Joint media release: Australia backs stronger coastlines and communities in the Pacific Joint media release: Australia backs stronger coastlines and communities in the Pacific 7 October 2026 Senator the Hon Penny Wong, Minister for Foreign Affairs The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Pat Conroy MP, Minister for Pacific Island Affairs Australia will invest $3 million to help Pacific island nations protect infrastructure and communities from the impacts of climate change through the Climate Infrastructure for Resilient Coastlines and Riverbanks (CIRCAR) project. CIRCAR works with local communities to protect coastlines and riverbanks. It blends nature-based solutions such as revegetation of eroding land, agriforestry and mangrove planting with structures including seawalls. With support from the Australian Government, the CIRCAR project is delivering solutions to protect four key infrastructure developments in the Pacific: The Wau-Bulolo Highway in Morobe Province in Papua New Guinea. Kings Road and Queens Road, in Central and Western Provinces in Fiji. The East Micronesia Cable landing site in Nanikaai, Tarawa, Kiribati. The landing site of the VAKA undersea telecommunications cable in Tuvalu being delivered through the Falepili Union. The CIRCAR project is supported by the Australian Government through the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP). The project is delivered by not-for-profit organisation Live & Learn Environmental Education in partnership with engineering firm ARUP. Quote attributable to Minister Wong: “Protecting critical infrastructure in the Pacific is important for the communities that rely on it, and for Australia. “This investment will help safeguard the roads, telecommunications links and other infrastructure that connect our region.” Quotes attributable to Minister Bowen: “Our support will help protect road and communication infrastructure in Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Kiribati and Tuvalu. “Without action, climate-driven damage would sever these vital links and cut off the communities that rely on them. “We're working with the Pacific to minimise the impacts of climate change and deliver resilient infrastructure where it's needed.” Quote attributable to Minister Conroy: “Pacific communities are leading the way on practical solutions to the challenges facing their coastlines and infrastructure. “By combining traditional knowledge with nature-based approaches—such as planting mangroves—and resilient infrastructure, this project will help protect communities, livelihoods and vital connections across our region.”

title: $7.29 million to strengthen Pacific energy security
text: $7.29 million to strengthen Pacific energy security $7.29 million to strengthen Pacific energy security 5 October 2026 Australia is strengthening Pacific energy sovereignty with a $7.29 million package to accelerate the region’s renewables rollout and a new agreement to support Vanuatu’s renewable energy transition. The funding will support engineers in developing grid modelling for Pacific countries to better assess and understand how to integrate renewables and support the Renewable Energy Commissioner and a team of technical experts to help drive project development and integration. It will establish an early careers program for energy professionals to lead the region’s renewable energy transition and enhance the capabilities and development opportunities for energy regulators across the Pacific. Australia has also signed a new Memorandum of Understanding with Vanuatu to help strengthen its renewable energy transition. Australian tools and expertise will help integrate more cheap, clean solar energy into Vanuatu’s grid while supporting a skilled local workforce. Additionally, the agreement will support workforce development, including supporting technical expertise transfer, building local capacity for infrastructure operations and maintenance, knowledge exchange with Australian institutions and workforce planning and assessments. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the new agreement would bolster Vanuatu’s energy sovereignty. “We’re supporting the Pacific’s renewable energy transition to help strengthen economic and energy security across the region,” Minister Bowen said. “Bringing more solar energy online will put downward pressure on prices while cutting emissions. “We’re proud to work with Vanuatu and our Pacific partners to access the benefits of renewable energy.” The funding package and agreement with Vanuatu are part of the $50 million Australia-Pacific Partnership for Energy Transition (APPET), an Australian Government initiative to support the region’s clean energy transition. Along with Vanuatu, Australia has signed APPET partnerships with Palau, the Republic of Marshall Islands, Tonga and Tuvalu.

title: Pre-COP sets course for Pacific-led climate action
text: Pre-COP sets course for Pacific-led climate action Pre-COP sets course for Pacific-led climate action 5 October 2026 ​The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of Negotiations for COP31 The Hon Lynda Tabuya, Fijian Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change The Hon Dr Maina Vakafua Talia, Tuvaluan Minister for Climate Change and the Environment The Hon Murat Kurum, COP31 President and Türkiye's Minister for Environmnet, Urbanisation and Climate Change Ministers and attendees from more than 50 countries gather for Pre-COP, co-hosted by Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia. Pre-COP is the last major Ministerial meeting before COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. The focus for Pre-COP is keeping 1.5°C within reach, accelerating the clean energy transition, elevating the ocean-climate nexus and unlocking finance for vulnerable countries. Ministers and attendees from more than 50 countries will gather in Fiji from Monday to help drive climate action and accelerate the clean energy transition at the 2026 Pacific Pre-COP meeting. Pre-COP is being co-hosted by Fiji and Australia on 5 to 8 October, while a special Leaders’ event on 5 to 6 October will take place in Tuvalu, a low-lying atoll on the frontlines of climate change. The meeting in Fiji will focus on keeping 1.5°C within reach, delivering cleaner and more secure energy, unlocking finance for vulnerable countries, safeguarding the ocean and protecting communities from worsening climate impacts. Disasters like glacier collapse, heatwaves and tropical storms are affecting millions of people across the world, but collective action is having a global impact. Before more than 190 countries signed the Paris Agreement in 2015, the world was on course for 4°C of warming, and International Energy Agency (IEA) figures showed renewables accounted for 23% of global energy generation. The world’s collective action has brought projected warming down to 2.6 degrees, and IEA figures indicate that renewables make up more than 34% of electricity generation worldwide. And momentum is only growing - renewables are now the cheapest form of energy generation globally and the fastest to deploy. It’s forecast that twice as much renewable capacity will be installed from 2025 to 2030 as was installed from 2019 to 2024. Pre-COP will help drive more of the collective action making a worldwide impact, with a focus on delivering cleaner and more secure energy, unlocking investment and strengthening climate resilience. Over four days of sessions and bilateral meetings, leaders and delegates will work to build climate and clean energy momentum and ensure every country can share in the jobs and economic benefits of the renewable energy transition. Alongside the meetings, Fiji will host the Vale ni Vanua – Knowledge Exchange program, highlighting youth climate leadership, presenting the latest climate science and showcasing solutions to climate impacts, including in maternal health, the ocean and agriculture. Quotes attributable to Fijian Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change, Lynda Tabuya: “The Pacific’s influence on global climate action has always been greater than its size. “Pre-COP will put Pacific priorities and solutions at the centre of global discussions and help turn commitments into practical action. This includes securing greater investment in blue economy solutions to protect our oceans, which are crucial for coastal and island nations on the frontline of climate change. “Renewable energy strengthens resilience, reduces fuel costs and supports sustainable development across our region.” Quotes attributable to Tuvaluan Minister for Climate Change and the Environment, Dr Maina Vakafua Talia: “The Leaders’ event will bring global decision-makers to the frontlines of climate change and will show both the impacts we face and the practical work underway to protect our communities. “Tuvalu is a low-lying atoll nation, just an average of two metres above sea level. The decisions we make at Pre-COP and COP31 will be felt by our communities first. “The outcomes from the Leaders’ event in Tuvalu and Pre-COP must help drive stronger ambition and action now.” Quotes attributable to President of Negotiations for COP31, Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “Our region is at the frontline of the climate crisis, where the effects of climate change are real and immediate. "Hosting Pre-COP in the Pacific is bringing the focus of the world to the impacts, opportunities and priorities in our region. “Australia will work closely with COP31 President Türkiye to secure practical outcomes that strengthen economies, improve energy security and build resilience, particularly in the Pacific.” Quotes attributable to COP31 President, Türkiye’s Minister for Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change, Murat Kurum: “We are coming to the Pacific to bear witness for how the tide is already pressing against the door. We want to remind world leaders that promises do not hold back the sea or shield homes from the fire. Only delivery can save us. The clock is now ticking as Pre-COP is the last major stop before the global summit in Antalya. The COP31 Presidency has an action plan ranging from electrification to zero waste, resilient cities and oceans, all supported by finance. We will spend this week knocking heads together to get everyone on board so that the world comes to Antalya ready to deliver results.”

title: Joint media release: Marinus Link: Delivering Australia's energy future
text: Joint media release: Marinus Link: Delivering Australia's energy future Joint media release: Marinus Link: Delivering Australia's energy future 2 October 2026 ​The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy Anne Urquhart MP, Member for Braddon The Albanese Government is getting on with building Marinus Link, a nation-building project that will create thousands of Tasmanian jobs, strengthen Australia’s energy security and help deliver cheaper, cleaner and more reliable electricity. The new undersea and underground electricity connection between Tasmania and Victoria will put Tasmania’s renewable energy resources at the heart of a stronger national electricity grid. Project Marinus, incorporating Marinus Link and the North West Transmission Developments being undertaken by TasNetworks, will deliver 750 megawatts of capacity, equivalent to the power needs of around 750,000 homes, and is expected to support around 2,400 jobs across Tasmania and Victoria. Marinus Link will allow electricity to flow both ways across Bass Strait. Tasmania will be able to import more low-cost solar and wind power when it is plentiful on the mainland, conserving water in its hydro dams, and export renewable electricity when it is needed most. For Tasmania, that means greater energy security during dry periods, new opportunities for renewable energy investment and better access to mainland markets. For the rest of the national grid, Project Marinus forms a critical part of our energy infrastructure, making better use of renewable energy across all states on the east coast, helping to keep our energy system reliable and putting downward pressure on electricity prices as ageing coal-fired power stations retire. The project is being delivered in partnership with the Tasmanian and Victorian governments, backed by concessional finance through the Albanese Government’s Rewiring the Nation program, delivered by the Clean Energy Finance Corporation. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “The previous Coalition Government spent years talking about what Marinus Link could deliver. We’re getting on with delivering it. “We’ve backed the project, secured the investment with the states and now we’re turning that ambition into jobs and construction.” “This connection works both ways. Tasmania can use cheap mainland solar and wind to save water in its dams, then send hydro power back when it’s needed most. “That’s good for Tasmania’s energy security and good for the rest of the national grid, delivering cleaner power where and when it’s needed. “This is what our energy plan is about: building the renewables, storage and connections needed for cheaper, cleaner and more reliable electricity.” Quotes attributable to Member for Braddon Anne Urquhart: “This is a big day for the North West Coast. Marinus Link means opportunities for local workers, local suppliers and businesses across our region. “I want young people growing up here to have more opportunities to learn a trade, build a career and raise a family without having to leave the Coast. “Our region has the skills and the people to help build Australia’s energy future. Today is an important step towards turning that opportunity into lasting benefits for our community.”

title: Expansion of rooftop solar scheme cuts upfront cost for businesses by 20%
text: Expansion of rooftop solar scheme cuts upfront cost for businesses by 20% Expansion of rooftop solar scheme cuts upfront cost for businesses by 20% 1 October 2026 From today, thousands of farmers, community organisations and small businesses across Australia, could save around 20 per cent on the installation costs of larger rooftop solar systems with the Albanese Government’s expanded Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme (SRES) now law. Mid-scale solar systems installed from today are eligible for support under the SRES where they meet scheme requirements. The expansion increases the maximum eligible solar system size from 100 kilowatts to 1 megawatt. The SRES has already supported over 4.5 million households and small businesses install solar. This expansion will help businesses, farms and community facilities install larger solar systems, putting more commercial roof space to work cutting energy bills. It will also help businesses switch equipment and operations to electricity and reduce exposure to international energy price shocks. To be eligible for the SRES, mid-scale solar PV systems will need to meet installer and product accreditation requirements and comply with state, territory and Commonwealth planning requirements, electrical safety regulations and network connection agreements. Details on eligibility are provided by the Clean Energy Regulator which administers the SRES. Lower energy costs can help manufacturers, farmers, retailers and transport and logistics businesses become more competitive. To complement the SRES expansion, the department is preparing a rule change request for the Australian Energy Market Commission aimed at making it easier for businesses to connect larger solar systems to the electricity network. For more information, please visit https://cer.gov.au/schemes/renewable-energy-target/small-scale-renewable-energy-scheme/small-scale-renewable-energy-systems Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: "This reform will reduce the upfront cost of installing a mid-scale solar system by around 20 per cent, making it easier for businesses and farmers to invest in cheaper, cleaner energy. "At a time when global energy markets remain volatile, more solar means lower exposure to international price shocks and greater energy security for Australian businesses. "We’ve seen what rooftop solar can do for household bills. We want more businesses to get those benefits too, from farms and factories to shops and warehouses. "Putting more solar on business rooftops means more Australian energy powering Australian industry, helping cut running costs and exposure to volatile fossil fuel prices.”

title: Visit to India and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to bolster energy security
text: Visit to India and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to bolster energy security Visit to India and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to bolster energy security 22 September 2026 Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen will travel to India and Saudi Arabia this week to strengthen Australia’s fuel security and work with international partners on global energy security. In India, Minister Bowen will meet with Ministerial counterparts and visit the Jamnagar oil refinery in Gujarat, the world’s largest oil refinery. The Minister will also convene a roundtable with clean energy industry representatives and deliver a key speech on electrification ahead of COP31 underscoring the importance of renewables to future global energy security and making all nations more resilient to the supply and price shocks of international disruptions. He will then travel to Saudi Arabia for direct meetings with Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud about the evolving situation overseas, including the closure of the East-West pipeline, and its implications for global energy security. The Minister will visit King Abdullah University of Science and Technology’s Centre of Excellence for Renewable Energy and Storage Technologies, highlighting the importance of electrification in future energy security, a key priority for COP31. Minister Bowen said Australia’s ongoing engagement with the world would help to deliver energy security both at home and abroad, enhanced through our role in leading negotiations at COP31. “What we are seeing in the Middle East is deeply concerning, and it is more important than ever that Australia engages with other nations on global energy security and fuel security back home, in our national interest,” Minister Bowen said. “That is why this week I will travel first to India, where I will meet Minister Yadav and visit the Jamnagar oil refinery in Gujarat, before travelling to Saudi Arabia for direct discussions with Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud. “Australia’s fuel supply remains secure and our strong relationships with international partners are an essential part of that work.”

title: Government extends fuel security settings
text: Government extends fuel security settings Government extends fuel security settings 19 September 2026 The Albanese Government will maintain flexibility in the domestic fuel market, by extending the temporary reduction of the baseline Minimum Stockholding Obligation for petrol and diesel until 31 January 2027. This precautionary action will continue to allow suppliers to hold 20 per cent less diesel and petrol in reserve if they commit to delivering more fuel into the domestic market and prioritising regional supply. The extension recognises higher fuel demand in regional Australia during the grain harvest and summer holiday travel season and gives industry ongoing flexibility to respond quickly in the event of another spike in demand. Since March, the temporary reduction has helped address supply chain pressures caused by periods of elevated demand, especially in regional Australia. Australia’s domestic reserves remain healthy, fuel continues to arrive as expected, and essential services, businesses and communities are operating as normal. Australia remains at level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan and we continue to have more fuel in Australia than we did at the beginning of the Iran war due to the Government’s swift and sensible actions to secure fuel supply, including: Securing more fuel internationally through the $7.5 billion Fuel and Fertiliser Security Facility, by partnering with Ampol, BP Australia, Viva, IOR and Freedom Fuels to help secure almost 800 million litres of additional diesel and 150 million litres of additional jet fuel, adding a further buffer to Australia’s fuel security. Building long term fuel resilience through the $3.2 billion Australian Fuel Security Reserve and increasing the Minimum Stockholding Obligation, to increase Australia’s reserves of diesel and jet fuel to 50 days Strengthening the Fuel Security Services Payment to ensure the future of Australia’s last two remaining oil refineries, and providing $10 million in 2026-27 to develop feasibility studies to expand our domestic refining capacity Securing Australia’s future fuel sovereignty through the $1.1 billion Cleaner Fuels Program, to boost the production of low-emission fuels in Australia, and working with industry on a market measure to drive demand and to reduce our reliance on imported fuels Our healthy domestic stockholdings have given Government confidence that this extension strikes the right balance of keeping fuel reserves in good supply, while maintaining flexibility in the local market should global fuel market conditions deteriorate amid unwelcome development. The Government is continuing to strengthen Australia’s fuel security and resilience, including through the recently released consultation paper on Australia’s Fuel Security and Resilience Package. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “Australia remains fuel secure – we continue to have more fuel in Australia than we did at the beginning of the war with 41 ships having arrived on our shores so far this month alone. “The Albanese Government is taking practical action to help keep fuel available when and where Australians need it, particularly during busy periods like harvest and the summer holidays. “This extension keeps fuel reserves in good supply, while maintaining flexibility in the local market. The most important thing Australians can continue to do is to buy the fuel they need – no more and no less. “Australia’s fuel outlook remains secure, and we will continue to work to secure more fuel for the immediate term, while making Australia more sovereign from international energy shocks in the future.”

title: Joint media release: $49 million boost to power Australian-made clean technology manufacturing
text: Joint media release: $49 million boost to power Australian-made clean technology manufacturing Joint media release: $49 million boost to power Australian-made clean technology manufacturing 18 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy Senator the Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation Alison Byrnes MP, Member for Cunningham The Albanese Government is backing Australian innovation and advanced manufacturing with a $49 million investment in Hysata to scale up production of its world-leading hydrogen electrolysers at Port Kembla, creating jobs in the Illawarra and strengthening Australia’s clean-energy industrial capability. Supported through the Australian Renewable Energy Agency’s (ARENA) Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund, the investment will help expand manufacturing capability in the Illawarra Region and strengthen Australia’s domestic clean-energy manufacturing capability. Electrolysers use electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen and are the key technology for producing renewable hydrogen. Hysata’s technology uses less electricity than conventional electrolysers, helping reduce the cost of renewable hydrogen for hard-to-abate industries such as steelmaking, fertiliser production and heavy transport. The project will strengthen Australia’s role in global clean-energy supply chains and support the Government’s Future Made in Australia agenda to build industrial capability, strengthen Australia’s economic resilience and create secure, well-paid jobs. The $98 million project will establish commercial-scale manufacturing of Hysata’s innovative electrolyser technology, which the company says can achieve system efficiency of around 95 per cent, compared with 65 to 75 per cent for other modern electrolysers. It is funded equally by the Albanese Government and Hysata, with the company matching the $49 million grant dollar for dollar from private capital and has helped crowd in more than $220 million of investment from global investors. The new manufacturing facility is helping turn Australian research into Australian-made technology and supporting the growth of Australia’s clean-energy manufacturing sector. The project will establish a 50 MW per annum manufacturing line, with capacity to increase to up to 200 MW per annum through continuous operations as demand grows. Developed from research originating at the University of Wollongong, the project is expected to create around 40 new manufacturing, engineering and technical jobs in the Illawarra and contribute to Australia’s growing clean-energy workforce. The project also supports Illawarra businesses through local supply chains, with Hysata spending $20 to $30 million with Australian suppliers each year, building a regional clean technology manufacturing ecosystem. Hysata also supports a training and skills development pathway delivered in partnership with the University of Wollongong and TAFE NSW Illawarra, helping to build the skilled workforce needed to manufacture Hysata’s world-leading electrolysers. In addition, the project includes deployment of early commercial-scale, megawatt-scale electrolyser systems. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen: “This project is a major jobs and economic opportunity for the Illawarra and helps ensure Australia makes more of the clean-energy technology the world needs. “Hysata’s electrolyser can help reduce the cost of hydrogen production and decarbonise energy-intensive sectors like steel, fertiliser and heavy transport. “Making electrolysers here in Australia is a huge opportunity to strengthen our manufacturing capability, back local innovation, create skilled jobs and seize a bigger share of the global clean-energy technology market.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Industry and Innovation, Tim Ayres: “This is exactly what a Future Made in Australia looks like: Australian research, Australian manufacturing and Australian workers building the technologies that will power the industries of the future. “Hysata is a great example of Australian ingenuity being turned into commercial opportunity, creating jobs in the Illawarra while strengthening Australia’s clean-energy manufacturing capability. “By backing innovative companies like Hysata to scale up, we’re helping ensure more world-leading technology is invented here, made here and exported to the world.” Quotes attributable to Member for Cunningham, Alison Byrnes: “Hysata is a true local success story – born from University of Wollongong research, backed by government and now delivering to customers around the globe. “This $49 million brings Australian Government investment in Hysata’s revolutionary electrolysers to more than $84 million in grant funding, alongside around $26 million of equity investment through the Clean Energy Finance Corporation, helping to scale up production and create even more skilled local jobs, with Hysata recently employing its 120th employee. “Together with our investments in Sicona, Gravitas, BlueScope and more, we’re building an advanced manufacturing network that is putting our region on the world stage. “The Illawarra has the skills, capability and drive to help power Australia’s clean-energy future, and the Albanese Labor Government is backing local jobs, local innovation and a Future Made in the Illawarra.”

title: Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes
text: Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes 17 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy Senator the Hon Katy Gallagher, Senator for the ACT The Hon Josh Wilson MP, Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy David Smith MP, Member for Bean A new digital tool will help Canberrans make their homes cheaper to run, healthier and more comfortable by offering a one-stop shop for home electrification upgrades. The ‘Go Electric’ tool will simplify the switch from gas to electricity by handling the key parts of the process – from expert advice and fixed-price quotes to installation and ongoing support – making it easier for Canberrans to get the most out of their next home upgrade. Residents of Canberra’s southern suburbs will be the first to try the digital platform in a trial involving up to 1,000 households led by home electrification company Electric Future and supported by $8.2 million from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA). As well as supporting upgrades to home heating, cooling and appliances, the trial will also help Canberrans make the most of electric vehicles, rooftop solar and home batteries. A key outcome of the project will be to demonstrate how home electrification can be delivered at scale, providing practical insights that can support more households to make the switch over time. The ACT-based trial builds on ARENA’s broader work supporting household and community energy innovation, with around 50 related initiatives funded since 2018 and more than $150 million invested in projects spanning home electrification, smart appliances, flexible energy use and technologies such as virtual power plants. These projects are helping households and communities take greater control of how they generate, store and use energy, cutting bills for homeowners, renters and public housing residents. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen: “Home upgrades can make a big difference to everyday life – not just to comfort and ease of use, but also to your hip pocket and the health of everyone under your roof. “But upgrading your home can feel daunting – you need to work out the right upgrades for your home and your needs, then find someone you trust to install them for the right price. “A one-stop shop providing expert advice, fixed-price quotes, trusted installers and ongoing support will help people make the best choices for themselves, their homes and their families – and gives them the confidence to get on with the job.” Quotes attributable to Senator for the ACT, Katy Gallagher: “Canberrans have been at the forefront of the transition to cleaner energy, and this investment builds on that progress. “Helping households use energy more efficiently and move away from gas is good for household budgets and good for our transition to a cleaner energy system. “This trial will also give us valuable evidence about how we can make electrification easier and more affordable for households at a much larger scale.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Josh Wilson: “The built environment is responsible for around a quarter of Australia’s emissions, so improving the energy performance of our homes is one of the most practical ways households can cut costs while contributing to climate action. “This project will help Canberrans make smarter choices about electrification and energy efficiency, creating healthier, more comfortable homes that are cheaper to run and better for the environment.” Quotes attributable to Member for Bean, David Smith: “South Canberra households will be the first to try this new one-stop shop, making it simpler to choose and install the right electric upgrades for their homes. “Canberrans are leading the country in switching to cleaner, cheaper-to-run homes, and this trial will help up to 1,000 local households take the next step. “Whether it’s better heating and cooling, electric appliances, rooftop solar or a home battery, this project will give local families trusted advice and support from start to finish.”

title: $30 million to help launch Australian clean energy start ups
text: $30 million to help launch Australian clean energy start ups $30 million to help launch Australian clean energy start ups 16 September 2026 The Albanese Government is backing homegrown early-stage startup companies with a $30 million boost to help turn Australian clean energy ideas into commercial technologies. Through its new Launchpad funding program, the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) will support startups developing new technologies in areas like low-cost solar, energy storage, distributed energy, transport, renewable hydrogen and green metals. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said Launchpad would help early-stage Australian energy and climate startups take the next step from developing an idea to bringing it to market. “Through the new Launchpad program, we’re backing Australian ideas, innovation and ingenuity with timely, targeted investment at the crucial early stage,” Minister Bowen said. “Australia has a strong research and innovation base, but a good idea needs backing to get off the ground. This funding will help energy and climate startups develop and demonstrate their technology and attract further investment. “With Launchpad, we’re helping Australian innovators turn their ideas into technologies that can cut emissions, strengthen Australian industry and create new opportunities for skilled jobs.” The program will allocate $15 million to support startups that are typically at an earlier stage than the companies that can apply for ARENA’s existing funding programs, with ARENA aiming to support between 15 to 30 startups. Successful applicants in the competitive funding round will receive $500,000, with a further $500,000 available for projects that require significant spending on equipment and infrastructure (up to $1,000,000 in total). Alongside direct support for Australian startups, Launchpad will provide a further $15 million to specialist ecosystem organisations that help climate and clean energy startups bring their technologies to market and grow their businesses. Successful applicants in this round can receive up to $5,000,000. Applications for the startup funding stream close on 28 October 2026, with funding for ecosystem support organisations available until the funding allocation is exhausted. More information on Launchpad is available on ARENA’s website.

title: Joint media release: Senate to endorse practical action on climate
text: Joint media release: Senate to endorse practical action on climate Joint media release: Senate to endorse practical action on climate 10 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Josh Wilson MP, Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy The protection of native forests and koala habitats is one step closer, with confirmation today that a majority of the Senate will oppose Coalition moves to disallow the Improved Native Forest Management (INFM) method. The INFM method gives state governments the option to support carbon sequestration alongside existing timber production and recreational uses, creating new opportunities for regional communities while delivering emissions reduction and environmental and biodiversity benefits. This is practical climate action that supports regional communities and should be allowed to pass through the Senate. The Albanese Government has made sensible adjustments to the implementation of the method. The measures agreed by the Albanese Government will enable the Clean Energy Regulator to give effect to the New South Wales Government's commitment to restrict the sale of Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) generated within the Great National Koala Park to a specified class of entities. This will apply only to projects under the INFM method and only where a state government chooses to opt into those requirements. In addition, the Assistant Minister has written to the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee (ERAC) seeking advice on variations to the INFM method, including: increasing the amount of forest that must be protected against established harvesting baselines before projects can receive any carbon credits, rising to 30 per cent for projects registered from 1 July 2030; and clarifying the definitions of plantation forest and native forest within the method. The ACCU Scheme is an important part of Australia's pathway to net zero emissions, helping drive emissions reductions while creating opportunities for landholders, First Nations peoples, regional communities and businesses. These are sensible, practical steps that further strengthen the method and build upon Australia's high-integrity carbon market. The Government awaits the Senate vote and getting on with delivering practical action on climate change and supporting our regions.

title: Joint media release: Securing more affordable gas for Australians
text: Joint media release: Securing more affordable gas for Australians Joint media release: Securing more affordable gas for Australians 10 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Madeleine King MP, Minister for Resources Senator the Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation, Minister for Science The Albanese Labor Government is taking another step forward to secure more affordable gas for households, business and industry with the release of the Domestic Gas Reservation legislative package for consultation. The Domestic Gas Reservation Bill 2026 will establish Australia’s first national Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme. This delivers on the Government’s commitment to secure gas supply for Australians and put downward pressure on domestic gas prices, by requiring gas exporters to supply a portion of the gas they produce to the domestic market. The Australian Government is reserving up to 20 per cent of gas exports for Australians, ensuring gas is more affordable and the domestic market is always modestly oversupplied. Exporters could provide up to 200 additional petajoules of gas a year, ensuring more than enough secure gas along with domestic production to meet new manufacturing demands. This is more than enough to avoid AEMO forecast possible shortfalls of up to 140 petajoules. This is a landmark Labor reform that will place significant downwards pressure on price paid by Australian gas consumers. The scheme ensures domestic customers can buy from a larger pool of gas, reducing the risk of tight market conditions driving price spikes, promoting long-term contracting and shielding them from global volatility. The licence application process will commence from 1 January 2027, with the Domestic Supply Obligation to commence from 1 January 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles. The Exposure Draft, released today, establishes a framework for how the reservation scheme is proposed to operate within a broader set of gas market reforms, including how costs will be recovered and the compliance and enforcement mechanisms available to the Regulator. The Government received more than 140 submissions in response to the Reservation’s Draft Design Framework – from gas producers and exporters, retailers, large industrial users, trade partners and state and territory governments. The Exposure Draft package ensures more affordable gas is available for Australian gas users, and builds on design features proposed by the Government earlier this year. Stakeholder feedback has been considered during the design of the legislation and market reforms to improve industry certainty and inform an Exposure Draft package that is predictable, transparent, and pro-investment while also delivering affordable, long term domestic gas supply. The Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme exposure draft and consultation materials are available now on the Department of Industry, Science and Resources Consultation Hub. Submissions will close on 24 September 2026. The Government welcomes further feedback to refine the draft legislation package before its proposed introduction to parliament later this year. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen MP: “For too long Australia has been in the perverse situation where despite being one of the world’s largest gas producers we had shortages and prices shocks at home. "We’re fixing that – with a system that secures the gas we need and pushes prices down for households and businesses. “Gas will be a crucial energy source as we transition to renewables, and cheaper gas can only help people and businesses to make the switch.” Quotes Attributable to Minister for Resources Madeleine King MP: “The Albanese Government is establishing the first national Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme because Australian households and businesses, quite rightly, expect to have access to affordable Australian gas. “This scheme requires gas exporters to make a portion of the gas they produce available to our domestic market, securing the gas Australian consumers and industry need, putting downward pressure on domestic gas prices, supporting jobs across the country, and growing the economy. “The Future Gas Strategy recognises that gas will remain an important part of Australia's energy mix and a critical partner to renewable energy through the transition to net zero. “By ensuring more Australian gas is available here at home, while maintaining our position as a trusted energy exporter, we are delivering a balanced approach that supports households, industry and long-term economic growth.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science Tim Ayres: “Securing affordable gas for Australian manufacturing and heavy industry supports good jobs, stronger supply chains and Australia’s domestic industrial capability. “A domestic gas reservation gives manufacturers and heavy industry access to the reliable and affordable energy they need to invest, produce and grow. “Gas continues to play an important role for industry and putting downward pressure on prices will help manufacturers remain globally competitive, secure existing jobs and create new opportunities for Australian workers.”

title: More EV chargers set for our suburbs
text: More EV chargers set for our suburbs More EV chargers set for our suburbs 8 September 2026 The Albanese Labor Government is making it easier for more Australians to choose cheaper-to-run electric vehicles, with a new round of rebates to install chargers at dealerships across suburban Australia. Dealers, repairers and mechanics can now claim up to $3,000 per EV charging plug, and 80 per cent of the cost of EV-specific workshop tools and equipment, up to a total of $50,000 per site. The expanded support is part of the Government’s DRIVEN program to help Australia’s automotive industry keep up with growing demand for electric vehicles. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the government was helping small businesses, dealerships, repairers and mechanics sell, service and repair more EVs across Australia, while supporting more chargers in suburban areas where EV sales have increased the most. “The Albanese Government’s New Vehicle Efficiency Standard is giving Australians access to more models, and now our investment in charging infrastructure is making it easier and cheaper for Australian families to choose an EV. “As electric vehicle sales overtake petrol car sales for the first time in Australia, now’s the time for dealerships, repairers and mechanics to update and upgrade their facilities so more Australian families can power up at a location closer to home,” Minister Bowen said. “Australians are voting with their wallets for a greater choice of cleaner, cheaper-to-run cars, reducing their exposure to international petrol price shocks.” "This is a welcome and practical expansion of the DRIVEN program at a time when dealers across Australia are investing millions in the tools, equipment and workshop upgrades required to service electric vehicles. “These additional funds will help dealers make that transition with confidence and ensure our customers continue to have access to safe, high-quality vehicle servicing and repairs," said James Voortman, CEO of Australian Automotive Dealer Association. The latest round of the DRIVEN program is open for applications until 30 April 2027, with rebates available for: EV charger purchase and installation – up to $3,000 per plug, within a category cap of $21,000 EV-specific workshop equipment and tools – up to 80% of eligible costs, including tools, protective equipment and workshop upgrades. This announcement comes as electric vehicle sales have overtaken petrol cars for the first time in Australia, as more drivers embrace cheaper running costs and greater choice. New vehicle sales figures for August show EV sales increased 171% compared with the same month last year, while battery electric vehicles outsold petrol cars, with 25,824 sales. Battery electric, plug-in hybrid and conventional hybrid vehicles together accounted for more than half of all new vehicle sales.

title: EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time
text: EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time 4 September 2026 Electric vehicles sales have overtaken petrol cars for the first time in Australia in August, as more drivers embrace cheaper running costs and greater choice. title: Joint media release: Pacific collaboration on climate and renewable energy powers ahead
text: Joint media release: Pacific collaboration on climate and renewable energy powers ahead Joint media release: Pacific collaboration on climate and renewable energy powers ahead 3 September 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy Australia and Palau are working together to super-charge the Pacific’s renewable energy transition, massively reducing reliance on diesel fuel. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and President of Palau Surangel Whipps Jr today visited Palau’s first large-scale solar power plant at Ngatpang on Babeldaob. The solar power plant has been financed by a $31.4 million package through the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP). Leaders marked the delivery of additional battery storage, a key milestone in a further $16.4 million AIFFP investment to upgrade Palau’s electricity grid. The upgrade will double energy storage capacity at the facility, increase renewable energy to 25 per cent of Palau’s total electricity generation and displace more than one million litres of diesel consumption annually. Leaders visited the facility to highlight how innovative partnerships can accelerate the shift to renewables and strengthen energy security and affordability. The visit followed the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders’ Meeting, where the Prime Minister announced a $1.89 million Australian contribution to support PIF Leaders’ proposal to create a Pacific Renewable Energy Commissioner. Once appointed, the Commissioner will support the region on a sustainable pathway towards a 100 per cent renewable energy future, including by advocating for more investment in renewables. This week's meeting of PIF builds climate change momentum ahead of the Pacific Pre-COP in Fiji and leaders event in Tuvalu. This critical meeting ahead of COP31 will amplify Pacific voices on the world stage, giving the region and Australia unprecedented influence over international climate negotiations. Prime Minister Albanese also announced Australia’s $25 million partnership with the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme over five years to advance shared climate and environmental priorities. Australia will also continue to support the Pacific’s longstanding international ocean leadership, contributing $1.7 million for the Office of the Pacific Ocean Commissioner and $1 million for the Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity initiative. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: “Today we saw firsthand how Australia and Palau’s close collaboration is delivering tangible benefits by helping provide cleaner, more reliable energy for homes, businesses and schools. “Palau has shown strong leadership on climate action and sustainable development, and Australia is proud to support those efforts. “Australia is committed to partnering with our Pacific family on climate action as we prepare to deliver the Pre-COP Leaders’ event in Fiji and Tuvalu later this year.” Quotes attributable to Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen: “We're backing a cleaner, more secure energy future for the Pacific. “Australia will provide $1.89 million to help establish the new Renewable Energy Commissioner for the Pacific, supporting investment in renewable energy, strengthening energy security and helping lower power costs across the region. “The Commissioner will help turn ambition into action by bringing together governments, investors and development partners to accelerate renewable energy projects and deliver lasting benefits for Pacific communities.” Quotes attributable to Pacific Island Affairs Minister Pat Conroy: “We recognise climate is the Pacific’s number one priority – and we’re committed to working with the region on the issues that matter. “We’re pleased to support this project which will accelerate the shift to renewables and help to make energy more reliable and affordable in Palau.”

title: Joint media release: $26 million boost for cleaner Australian-made iron technology
text: Joint media release: $26 million boost for cleaner Australian-made iron technology Joint media release: $26 million boost for cleaner Australian-made iron technology 2 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Madeleine King MP, Minister for Resources Senator The Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation The Hon Anne Aly MP, Minister for Small Business and International Development The Hon Josh Wilson MP, Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Albanese Government is backing Australian innovation and manufacturing with $26 million for technology that provides a pathway for Pilbara ore in lower-emissions iron production. The Government is supporting Perth-based Element Zero with funding through the Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund, administered by the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA), to pilot technology transforming Australian iron ore into high purity iron using an electricochemical process. Element Zero’s $53.7 million project could help Australia capture more value from its world-class iron ore resources, build specialist skills and strengthen Australian industrial supply chains. Iron and steel production is one of the world's largest industrial sources of emissions, as conventional ironmaking typically uses coal and other carbon-based materials to convert iron ore into iron. Element Zero's project will test whether an alternative process – electrochemical ironmaking, which is powered by electricity and uses molten salts – could produce lower-emissions iron efficiently without relying on coal. The pilot will test a process designed to operate at around 400 to 450°C, significantly lower than temperatures typically used in traditional ironmaking. The project will be delivered in two stages. The first stage will involve a pilot plant capable of producing around one tonne of iron per day. Subject to a formal review, the second stage will scale production up to 10 tonnes per day. The pilot will test different types of Australian iron ore, including hematite-goethite, and help demonstrate the technology’s potential to Australian and international steelmakers. This investment is part of ARENA’s efforts to build a portfolio of projects, also including hydrogen-based approaches, aimed at unlocking viable pathways for producing green iron at scale. Green metals is a key priority under the Albanese Government’s Future Made in Australia agenda, helping Australia leverage our world-class iron ore resources, and industrial capability to make more things here, capture more value from our resources, and secure new opportunities as global demand for lower-emissions industrial products grows. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “Australia has the iron ore the world needs and some of the best renewable energy resources in the world – the opportunity is to bring those advantages together and make more things here. “This investment backs Australian technology that could add more value to Australian iron ore, support Australian manufacturing and help cut emissions from one of the hardest parts of the global economy to decarbonise.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Resources Madeleine King: “Australia's iron ore industry has long been a cornerstone of our economy, and projects like this are helping position it for the future by developing new ways to turn our world-class resources into higher-value products here in Australia.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Industry and Innovation Tim Ayres: “This project is exactly what Future Made in Australia is about: turning Australian resources and Australian innovation into new industrial opportunities. “This investment helps to develop new ways to turn more of our iron ore into higher-value products here at home, creating jobs, capability and economic resilience in the process.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy Josh Wilson: “Ironmaking is one of the most emissions-intensive parts of steel production, which is why investing in cleaner ways to make iron is such an important opportunity for Australian industry, particularly here in Western Australia.” Quotes attributable to Member for Cowan, Anne Aly: “Western Australia has powered our economy for generations, and projects like this are about making sure we’re also at the forefront of the industries and jobs of the future. “Backing WA companies to develop new technologies means more opportunities to turn our world-class resources into higher-value products right here at home.”

title: Renewables continue to lower Australia’s emissions
text: Renewables continue to lower Australia’s emissions Renewables continue to lower Australia’s emissions 28 August 2026 New data shows Australia’s climate pollution is down 1.6% as solar, wind and batteries continue to replace more expensive coal and gas generation in Australia’s electricity grids. The latest Quarterly Update of Australia’s National Greenhouse Gas Inventory estimates 455.6 million tonnes of emissions over the year to March 2026 – a 7.5 million tonne drop over the previous year. Record high generation from renewables drove a 5.6 million tonne cut in electricity emissions as it continued to displace coal and gas-fired generation. That represents a 3.7% decline. This comes as the Clean Energy Regulator confirms the June quarter has set new records, with over 1 GW of rooftop solar installed and 1.8 GW of large-scale solar final investment decisions. Fugitive and stationary energy emissions also fell by a combined 1.7 million tonnes, due to reductions in natural gas venting, underground coal mining and oil and gas extraction. Electricity emissions are falling steadily as Australians add more batteries and renewables at a household, community and grid level, driven by policies like the Cheaper Home and Community Batteries programs. The trend is expected to continue as the Capacity Investment Scheme supports an additional 26 GW of solar and wind generation across the country, backed by 14 GW of new clean energy storage. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the results showed the practical benefits of building Australia’s cleaner, cheaper and more reliable energy system. “The latest quarterly update is further proof that what’s better for the planet is better for your pocket; more of the cheapest form of new energy, more storage to back it up, and lower emissions as a result,” Minister Bowen said. “With over 4 million household solar systems and more than half a million home batteries supported by our Cheaper Home Batteries Program, we’re seeing the results of consistent and considerable cuts in electricity grid emissions. “Meanwhile the Coalition and One Nation are promising higher bills and higher pollution – that's not the real change Australia needs.” More domestic air travel and diesel road transport drove the 0.2% increase in overall transport emissions, which was tempered by falling petrol use as more Australians move to electric vehicles. The small increase in transport emissions follows drops in the years to September and December 2025, with levels still below the record high in the year to December 2024 – the last period before the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard came into effect. “Australia is turning the corner when it comes to stubborn transport pollution – that's good news for motorists as more drivers embrace cheaper to run cars thanks to our policies delivering more choice to the market.” The quarterly update of Australia’s emissions is available at https://www.dcceew.gov.au/climate-change/publications/national-greenhouse-gas-inventory-quarterly-update-march-2026

title: Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero
text: Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero 27 August 2026 Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen today hosted China’s Minister of Ecology and Environment, Huang Runqiu, for the 10th Australia-China Ministerial Dialogue on Climate Change at Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park. Together, Australia and China are unlocking the economic opportunities of the global clean energy transformation – empowering households to take control of their energy bills through electrification and helping nations make their energy grids more secure and reliable. Ministers discussed the economic opportunities of the global shift to net zero and the opportunity to strengthen energy security while transitioning away from fossil fuels. They underscored the importance of accelerating climate action to achieve net zero by or around mid-century, in keeping with the science. Further to the discussion between Prime Minister Albanese and Premier Li in April, and subsequent Ministerial exchanges, the Dialogue emphasised the importance of both countries working to ensure energy security for both nations, including the continued flow of liquid fuels. With Australia leading COP31 negotiations, Ministers agreed to work together in the lead up to and at COP31 to support global emissions reduction goals, furthering the shared aim of building trade and economic opportunities in both countries and around the world. Ministers Bowen and Huang discussed the benefits of increasing electrification, including economic growth, energy security, job creation and improved public health and downward pressure on household budgets by helping homes take charge of their energy bills. Ministers also welcomed efforts to strengthen emissions accounting and adaptation policy initiatives and agreed to continue our exchange in these areas in the national interest of both countries. Engagement with Beijing on climate change is in line with Australia's broader policy on China of cooperating where we can, disagreeing where we must and engaging in our national interest. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “By strengthening understanding and cooperation with one of the world’s largest economies, we are able to strengthen global energy security and help insulate households from global price shocks, in our national interest. “In leading global climate negotiations, Australia is driving practical international action and working with our major trade partners to unlock the economic opportunities of electrification, which is putting downward pressure on energy bills. “I look forward to working constructively with all our international partners, including China, to accelerate electrification and the energy transition in the lead-up to COP31.”

title: Joint media release: New Capacity Investment Scheme tender to include Developer Rating Scheme
text: Joint media release: New Capacity Investment Scheme tender to include Developer Rating Scheme Joint media release: New Capacity Investment Scheme tender to include Developer Rating Scheme 25 August 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Josh Wilson MP, Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Albanese Government is backing Western Australia’s clean energy future by bringing forward another 1.8 gigawatts of renewable generation in Western Australia, enough to power around 1 million West Australian households, through the next round of the Capacity Investment Scheme (CIS), helping deliver the reliable and affordable power needed for the state’s growing economy. Registrations open on 25 August, with bids opening on 27 August alongside the release of the tender guidelines. The Tender will also be the first to require participation in the Government’s new Developer Rating Scheme (DRS). Proponents must have commenced the DRS assessment process to apply for CIS Tender 11. Tender 11 builds on the strong momentum already being delivered through the CIS, bringing forward the new generation and storage needed to keep the grid reliable and put downward pressure on power prices. Consistent with previous WEM tenders, projects will be required to participate in Western Australia's Reserve Capacity Mechanism, helping maintain a reliable electricity supply as more renewable energy enters the grid. Tender 11 will also place a stronger emphasis on projects being ready and able to deliver, including their ability to attract financing. Together, CIS tenders in Western Australia announced this year have already backed 10 projects delivering 1.9 GW of renewable generation and 482 MW of storage, delivering enough renewable electricity for more than 1 million WA households and enough storage to support more than 400,000 households during peak demand. Two projects supported through an earlier CIS dispatchable tender in WA, totalling enough energy to power over 100,000 homes (250 MW), have already signed agreements and commenced construction. The DRS is operated independently by Equifax, giving landholders and local communities greater transparency about the track record, capability and conduct of renewable energy developers and transmission companies Accredited companies that meet minimum standards across all seven criteria can be listed on a public register and receive a community engagement star rating, giving communities better information about developers with strong performance and engagement practices. Going forward it will also be a pre-requisite in CIS tenders, for developers to have started the DRS assessment process. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen “Western Australia needs more power as its economy and population grow, and this tender will bring forward another 1.8 GW of new generation to help deliver it “We’re also lifting the bar for developers – if you want Commonwealth backing through this tender, you need to show you’re serious about working properly with communities and landholders. “More renewable generation means more reliable supply and more competition, helping put downward pressure on power prices for WA households and businesses.” “Across Australia, the Capacity Investment Scheme is already supporting more than 100 projects, demonstrating the scale and pace of investment being driven by the Government's plan for cleaner, cheaper and more reliable energy.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy Josh Wilson “Western Australia has a critical role to play in Australia's clean energy future, and this tender will help bring forward the generation capacity needed to support the state's growing economy and population. “By placing a stronger emphasis on deliverability and financing capability, we're ensuring projects supported through the Capacity Investment Scheme are well positioned to be built and provide energy when it's needed. “We're ensuring First Nations communities have meaningful opportunities to share in the benefits of the energy transformation through dedicated equity and revenue-sharing arrangements.”

title: Record clean energy build strengthens reliability outlook
text: Record clean energy build strengthens reliability outlook Record clean energy build strengthens reliability outlook 25 August 2026 A record pipeline of new generation and storage is putting Australia on a stronger path to maintain electricity reliability as ageing coal-fired power stations retire, according to latest National Electricity Market (NEM) Electricity Statement of Opportunities (ESOO) report, an annual 10-year reliability outlook published by the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO). Previous ESOOs under the Coalition repeatedly forecast substantial reliability gaps as ageing coal generators retired. The 2026 ESOO shows the pipeline of generation and storage needed to maintain reliability has strengthened materially, backed by a strong rollout of new renewable generation, batteries, transmission and growing investment by households in rooftop solar and battery storage. Around 40 GW of new generation and storage is now committed or anticipated, with a further 33 GW supported by government programs. For context, the entire NEM is 77 GW today. Around 9 GW of new capacity was added over the past year, a new yearly record, while 24 GW has moved into committed or anticipated status since last year’s ESOO. Importantly, AEMO identifies no reliability gaps in 2027-28 or 2029-30, making clear continued investment and timely delivery will be needed as electricity demand grows and more ageing coal generation retires. AEMO says “ consumer and market investments are strengthening the pathway to maintain reliability ”, with the development pipeline having “strengthened materially” over the past year. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the report showed Australia’s energy transformation was gathering pace. "This is what getting on with the energy transition looks like, with record amounts of new generation and storage being built and connected, strengthening reliability as ageing coal-fired power stations approach their scheduled retirement dates," Minister Bowen said. "Our Capacity Investment Scheme, investment in long overdue transmission upgrades and rolling out over 500,000 Cheaper Home Batteries are just some of the things we’re doing to deliver the power Australia needs, keeping the lights on while putting downward pressure on energy costs. "There is more work to do and AEMO is clear we need to keep building, but this report shows the pipeline is strong and reliability is improving." The report also highlights the increasingly important contribution households are making to the grid through rooftop solar and batteries. AEMO says household energy resources like home batteries are reducing demand on the grid and the amount of generation required in the evening. Electricity demand is forecast to grow over the coming decade as households and businesses electrify and new industries expand, including significant growth in data centres. AEMO forecasts data centre electricity consumption could grow from around 3 per cent of the National Energy Market today to almost 15 per cent over the next decade, reinforcing the need for large new energy users to provide the additional renewable generation and firming required to meet their demand with them.
